Title: Tourism boom pushes limits of Athens air traffic control
Article:
GREEN arrows representing tourist-laden jets pile up on the screens of the Athens air traffic controllers, a puzzle to solve at the height of tourist season.
"Look at this sky, it's crazy, there's no room for any more planes!" exclaimed Olga Toki, vice-president of the Association of Air Traffic Controllers of Greece.
There is no doubt that this is a busy summer for the overworked air traffic controllers.
In the low season, Greece's airports typically handle between 1,000 and 1,500 flights per day, according to the Greek Civil Aviation Authority.
In the first week in July, by contrast, they handled an average of 2,700 flights per day.
Overall traffic in southeast Europe, which includes Greek airspace, has risen about 40 per cent from 2019, according to Eurocontrol, the air navigation safety organisation.
That underlined a boom in tourist arrivals in Greece, which last year were 23 percent higher than the 2019 pre-Covid peak, at 38 million, in a country of around 10 million people.
Even before the summer rush, nerves were on edge; a Jan 4 breakdown in the communication system linking air traffic controllers and aircraft had laid bare a glaring weakness.
Controllers could see the planes on their screens but were unable to hear or talk with the pilots.
The authorities had to close Greek airspace for hours, causing chaos, with a chain of cancellations and diversions to neighbouring countries.
The crisis was the catalyst for the announcement of a renovation programme costing around 300 million euros (US$350 million), including the installation of new digital communication systems.
The systems began to be installed in mid-August. The entire project – which includes replacing ageing radar – is supposed to be completed by 2028.
The European Commission last year brought a case before the Court of Justice of the European Union reproaching Greece for failing to bring its navigation procedures in line with the global Performance-Based Navigation (PBN) standard.
For those charged with keeping travellers safe, meanwhile, it is a sober responsibility. In the control room, the map of Greece is divided into 10 sectors, each managed by a controller assisted by an aide.
"In summer, we are desperately short of staff," explained shift supervisor Giorgos Stamoulakatos.
"There are 154 of us controllers; we need 250," he estimated.
[[nid:1517662]]
New controllers have been hired – 92 in 2025 and 77 in 2026 – but each newcomer must be trained for five years.
Areti Anastopoulos, an air traffic controller for more than 30 years, helps approaching pilots to line up their planes, one behind the other, before they touch down on the tarmac. Her husky voice is familiar to pilots in Greek skies – as are her outbursts.
"Normally, we guide around 20 pilots over the course of an hour. But right now, 40 are in the queue. Inevitably, delays build up," she lamented.
"Thirty-three planes landed in one hour. Twenty-eight is supposed to be our limit!"
More than once, she said, she has had to order planes to slow down or alter their trajectories to avoid accidents.
"What we're doing here is a superhuman attempt to keep everyone safe," she said.
The Middle East war has made the problem worse, adding around 300 extra flights crossing Greek airspace every day – nearly six per cent of daily traffic – according to Eurocontrol.
"In addition to commercial flights, we monitor incursions by Turkish planes and drones. Greece's geographic position increases our workload," Toki said.
In the passenger terminal, Jose Lopez arrived recently from Barcelona, 30 minutes late.
"That's not shocking in the middle of August. I've already experienced much worse delays," he said.
Christos, a valet at a major Athens hotel, was more irritated.
"Delays are more frequent than last year. I've had to wait up to seven hours for American clients," he said.
"Tourism is our added value in Greece," acknowledged controller Anastopoulos. "But more planes without more investment is not possible."
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Shein to pay up to US$3.5bil to select pre-IPO investors around Hong Kong listing
Article:
HONG KONG: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein will pay up to US$3.5 billion to selected existing investors - almost twice the fresh capital it is seeking in an IPO - to help compensate them for a sharp slide in its valuation, its prospectus showed on Monday.
The investors entitled to the payments in cash and extra shares include entities linked to Boyu Capital, Tiger Global, General Atlantic, Thrive Capital, Mubadala, Brookfield and others, the filings showed.
They hold Shein's late-stage funding shares - Series pre-D, Series D and Series D plus preferred - which carry protections triggered by an IPO below the prices paid in earlier funding rounds.
The broader group of preferred shareholders also includes Sanabil Private Equity, Coatue, D1 Capital, DST Asia, Reliance Retail, Coppel Capital, and Claure Group.
The prospectus for its listing in Hong Kong does not disclose how much each investor will receive.
The payments are nearly double the up to HK$13.86 billion (US$1.77 billion) that Shein aims to raise by selling about 280 million shares in its IPO, based on the top end of its indicated price range.
Shein's proposed IPO price of HK$47.60 to HK$49.50 per share would value the company at up to about US$27 billion.
That is below the private valuations attached to the eligible funding rounds of US$60.5 billion for the Series pre-D round in 2022, US$98.2 billion for the Series D round later that year and US$64 billion for the Series D plus round in 2023.
Shein said it could pay up to US$2.2 billion in cash under the conversion adjustment protections, assuming the IPO is priced at the bottom of the range.
It will also issue 19.6 million additional shares to eligible holders at no cost.
Separately, Shein also agreed to make about US$1.33 billion in payments to holders of Series pre-D, D and D plus preferred shares.
That includes about US$1.1 billion, payable in three instalments by March 31, June 30 and Sept 30. A further estimated US$230.4 million, which accrues until the IPO closes, will be paid within 15 business days after IPO completion.
Shein said the payments will be funded from its own financial resources. Holders of Shein's older Series A, Series B, Series C and Series C plus preferred shares are not covered, the prospectus showed.

Title: Police review CCTV footage in fatal Putrajaya cycling accident probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Police are reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage around the scene of an accident in which
two cyclists were killed
after being hit by a car at Km9.0 of Jalan Persiaran Selatan, Presint 5, here last Thursday.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed said the cause of the incident is still under investigation, and police require further verification through the CCTV footage.
"Investigating officers will go to the Putrajaya Corporation's Putrajaya Command Centre today to review the CCTV footage from the scene for further action," he said when contacted today.
He added that statements from four individuals have been recorded to assist in the investigation, involving two next of kin, the car driver, and a road contractor.
It was previously reported that police had recorded a statement from the driver, a man in his 40s, though he was not detained.
In the incident at 10.15pm last Thursday, cyclists Mohd Hilmi Tahar, 48, and Syazwan Zharif Abdul Karim, 30, died at the scene.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fadhlina receives Datuk Seri title, Ziana Zain now a Datuk
Article:
AYER KEROH: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek leads 1,328 recipients of Melaka state honours, appointments and medals in conjunction with the birthday of Yang Dipertua Negeri Melaka Tun Dr Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam today.
Fadhlina will receive the Darjah Gemilang Seri Melaka (DGSM), which carries the title Datuk Seri.
[[nid:1517642]]
Also receiving the same award are Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah; Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail; Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman; Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris; Petronas Downstream executive president and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Sazali Hamzah; and Datuk Seri Megat Zulkarnain Omardin, who is Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's political secretary and Malaysian National Silat Federation (Pesaka) president.
Meanwhile, 56 individuals were conferred the Darjah Cemerlang Seri Melaka (DCSM), which carries the title Datuk Wira.
They include Benut assemblyman and Umno executive secretary Datuk Wira Mohd Sumali Reduan; Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Wira M Kumar; National Solid Waste Management Department director-general Datuk Wira Dr Mohd Azhar Abd Hamid; and Melaka police chief Datuk Wira Dzulkhairi Mukhtar.
A total of 14 recipients were conferred the Darjah Mulia Seri Melaka (DMSM), which carries the title Datuk, including Sabah Deputy Speaker Datuk Al Hambra Juhar; High Court judge Datuk Suria Kumar Durairaj Johnson Paul; and Third Infantry Division commander Major General Datuk Sani S Omar.
Another 189 recipients were conferred the Darjah Pangkuan Seri Melaka (DPSM), which also carries the title Datuk.
[[nid:1517641]]
They include Media Prima TV Networks' Group Editor for News and Current Affairs Datuk Azhari Muhiddin; Merlimau-born singer Datuk Siti Roziana Zain, better known as Ziana Zain; and Broadcasting Department director-general Datuk Ashwad Ismail.
[[nid:1517640]]
Five individuals were appointed Justices of the Peace (JP), while 106 recipients were conferred the Darjah Seri Melaka (DSM).
The Bintang Cemerlang Melaka (BCM) was also awarded to 151 recipients, followed by the Bintang Khidmat Terpuji (BKT) to 244 recipients, Pingat Jasa Kebaktian (PJK) to 386 recipients, Pingat Bakti Masyarakat (PBM) to 161 recipients and Pingat Khidmat Lama (PKL) to five recipients.
State Secretary Datuk Wira Salhah Salleh said the honours reflected the state's appreciation for individuals who had rendered service, contributions and dedication in various fields, while playing a role in the state's development and well-being.
She said the 2026 Melaka State Honours, Appointments, Decorations and Medals Investiture Ceremony was coordinated with all relevant agencies and conducted in accordance with established procedures and protocols to ensure the smooth running, security and comfort of recipients and guests throughout the ceremony.
"The investiture ceremony will be held in three sessions, beginning today, followed by the second and third sessions on Wednesday," she said.

Title: Two Datuk remanded for 3 more days over alleged land abuse
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Magistrates' Court here today granted a three-day remand extension for two Datuk, including a Datuk who is a government agency chairman, over alleged abuse of power involving government agency land.
Magistrate Nurhanisah S H Sahul Hamid granted the extension after the duo were brought to court at about 9.30am.
Besides the 53-year-old Datuk who chairs a government agency, the other Datuk, in his 40s, is a developer.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had sought four days, but the court granted three, with the duo expected to be released on Wednesday.
Three others previously remanded, including the Datuk chairman's brother, sister-in-law and a developer, have been released on bail.
The five were initially remanded for four days last Friday.
Speaking to reporters after the proceedings, lawyer Dr Shamsher Singh Thind, who represented the Datuk chairman, said the prosecution had cited concerns that his client could interfere with witnesses and documents.
"The reason for the remand is normal — because he is the chairman, they don't want him to interfere with other witnesses, and there are piles of documents," he said.
The investigation centres on alleged abuse of position in the sale of land in Seberang Prai Selatan in 2015.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 20 Chinese citizens remanded for four days in love scam probe
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Twenty Chinese citizens have been remanded for four days to assist in investigations into a suspected love scam syndicate targeting victims in China.
Magistrate Nurhanisah S. H. Sahul Hamid issued the remand order until Thursday to allow police to conduct further investigations.
All 20 suspects, aged between 19 and 41, were represented by lawyer Cheah Eng Soon.
The suspects were detained during a raid at a three-storey house in Solok Sungai Emas, Batu Feringghi, at 7.05pm yesterday.
They are suspected of involvement in a love scam syndicate targeting victims in China using Telegram for online fraud activities.
Police also seized more than 100 mobile phones of various brands, three laptops, several notebooks, and other equipment believed to have been used in the syndicate's operations.
Some of the suspects are also believed to be without valid travel documents.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad is expected to issue a press statement on the case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 10 injured in Subang Jaya theme park roller coaster accident
Article:
SUBANG JAYA: Ten people were injured in a roller coaster accident at a theme park here on Saturday night.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said the incident occurred at 9pm and involved 22 riders, comprising Malaysians and foreign tourists aged between 11 and 44.
He said 10 of the riders suffered injuries and were taken to medical facilities around Subang Jaya for treatment.
"All the victims suffered minor injuries, and there were no fatalities," he said in a statement today.
Wan Azlan said police received a report on the incident at 11.45am yesterday and investigations are underway to determine the cause of the accident.
Two videos linked to the incident have since gone viral on social media.
One video, believed to have been recorded immediately after the incident, shows people carrying a victim on a stretcher near a section of track surrounded by trees.
A second video, recorded during the day, shows a crowd gathered near an amusement ride area at the theme park, with several police personnel and theme park staff walking away from one of the rides.
Those with information can contact the Subang Jaya district police headquarters at 03-7862 7100, with police assuring that the identities of informants will be kept confidential.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: "Just come and see me," Indira's plea for missing daughter
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: For 17 years, M. Indira Gandhi has lived with the same unanswered question: where is her daughter, Prasana Diksa?
After another court battle ended today, the answer remains elusive.
The kindergarten teacher was visibly disappointed after the Court of Appeal dismissed her appeal in her RM100 million suit against the police and government, but stressed that the case had never been about money.
"This is not about getting compensation. It is about finding Prasana.
"She has been missing for 17 years," she said, struggling to hold back tears when met after the hearing.
The 52-year-old's voice carried the weight of nearly two decades of searching, legal battles, and waiting for the daughter who was just 11 months old when she was taken by her former husband, K. Pathmanathan, on March 31, 2009.
With Prasana set to turn 18 this year, Indira said she continues to hold on to hope that her daughter will one day reach out to her.
"I hope I can find her as soon as possible. There has been no indication that she has tried to contact me.
"If she does, it would be better. I hope she can contact me. That is the only way.
"All I want is to see her. I have done everything... I went to court, I went to the police... Everything, but it was not enough.
"Just come and see me. Whatever she wants to be or whoever she wants to be with is not an issue. I just want to see her," she said.
Earlier, the Court of Appeal unanimously dismissed Indira's appeal seeking damages over the police's alleged failure to locate Pathmanathan and recover Prasana.
Although the court found material deficiencies in police evidence concerning efforts to execute the warrant of committal against Pathmanathan, it ruled that Indira had failed to prove that any specific police omission probably caused her loss or prolonged her separation from Prasana.
The panel, comprising justices Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan, Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid, also stressed that the warrant against Pathmanathan remains unexecuted and that the police's continuing statutory duty to execute it has not diminished with the passage of time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China evacuates tens of thousands as rain from Typhoon Narra lashes southwest
Article:
BEIJING: Torrential rain triggered by Typhoon Narra caused widespread flooding across China's southwestern Guangxi region over the weekend, forcing tens of thousands of people to relocate as forecasters warned of more downpours in the days ahead.
Some 54,000 people have been relocated because of the flooding, including 8,087 moved to emergency shelters, state broadcaster CCTV said.
Water levels at 20 monitoring stations on 15 rivers exceeded warning thresholds.
Aerial footage from CCTV showed brown floodwaters engulfing parts of Chongzuo city, with roads and clusters of low-rise buildings submerged.
Rescuers could be seen wading through knee-deep floodwaters while using rubber boats to evacuate stranded residents from inundated neighbourhoods.
Typhoon Narra has lingered over the Beibu Gulf, also known as the Gulf of Tonkin, in the northwestern part of the South China Sea for several days, bringing heavy rain to Guangxi and the nearby provinces of Hainan and Guangdong.
Heavy rain is expected to persist across parts of southern China through Wednesday, with areas of Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan and Fujian forecast to receive torrential rain, CCTV said.
China postponed the launch of its uncrewed Chang'e-7 lunar mission, which had been expected as early as Monday from Hainan's Wenchang Space Launch Site, saying the spacecraft did not "meet launch conditions."
The National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand, which has a scientific payload aboard the mission, said the delay was caused by the typhoon.
China Manned Space Agency did not respond immediately to a request for comment on the cause of the delay.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Narcotics policeman in Kelantan investigated over alleged affair
Article:
KUALA KRAI: A narcotics policeman in Kelantan is being investigated over allegations that he had an affair with a married woman.
State police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the probe was initiated after a 30-second video clip purportedly involving the policeman went viral on social media yesterday.
"Yes, I can confirm that we have conducted an internal investigation into the policeman.
"The policeman's statement has also been recorded," he said when contacted.
Mohd Yusoff said police would await the outcome of the internal investigation before taking further action.
The 30-second video, which was widely shared on social media, showed several villagers gathered outside a house in Kuala Krai.
A car, believed to belong to the policeman, was seen parked outside the house.
More than 10 people were seen waiting near the house.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's leading index rises 1.3pct on trade, chip demand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's leading index posted an annual growth of 1.3 per cent to 114.8 points in June, reflecting the strengthening of Malaysia's trade activities, said the Statistics Department.
The index was driven by a surge in real imports of other basic precious and other non-ferrous metals (35.1 per cent) as well as real imports of semiconductors (14.2 per cent).
"This scenario is in line with the strengthening of Malaysia's trade activities, particularly sustained demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) products," said the department in a statement today.
However, the overall performance was partly offset by declines in several components, notably the number of new companies registered.
On a monthly basis, the index also recorded a marginal increase of 0.02 per cent, contributed mainly by real imports of other basic precious and other on-ferrous metals (0.8 per cent).
Looking ahead, the department said that the long-term smoothed trend of the leading index remained below 100 points.
"Nevertheless, the economy is expected to continue growing, supported by resilient domestic demand and continued expansion in investment activities.
"At the same time, an increasingly dynamic global economic landscape and the recovery in international trade are expected to continue supporting Malaysia's economic growth," it added.
For current economic performance, the coincident index rose 2.6 per cent year-on-year with 131.6 points underpinned by strong growth in all components, particularly the real contributions, Employees Provident Fund (16 per cent) and the volume index of retail trade (4.1 per cent).

Title: E-hailing driver charged with attempted murder after setting Kepong woman on fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An e-hailing driver pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to a charge of attempting to murder a lottery outlet worker by setting her on fire, leaving her with severe injuries.
Ang Kam Tong, 59, claimed trial after the charge was read out before judge Datin Surita Budin.
"Not guilty," he said from the dock.
According to the charge sheet, Ang is accused of attempting to murder Gan Siew Teen, 62, by dousing her with petrol and setting her alight at a lottery outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong at 7.51am on Aug 9, causing her to suffer severe third-degree burns.
The accused was charged under Section 307(1) of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 20 years upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shakila Mohd Shariff appeared for the prosecution and urged the court to deny bail, citing the severity of the victim's third-degree burns and a police report indicating the accused had attempted to flee during his arrest.
However, lawyer Lee Keng Fatt, representing the accused, applied for bail.
"The accused is an e-hailing driver with no fixed income, is unmarried and has siblings who may be able to stand as sureties," he said.
The court subsequently allowed the accused to be released on RM15,000 bail with one surety and fixed Sept 25 for mention and submission of documents.
During
the incident
, Gan was unlocking the premises when Ang approached her, splashed petrol over her body, ignited a lighter, and threw it at her before fleeing on foot.
Gan, who lives within walking distance of her workplace, suffered burns on her face, neck, arms and body.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pax Silica makes navigating global critical minerals supply war harder
Article:
Two Asean countries, the Philippines and Singapore, had signed the US-led Pax Silica Declaration, which set up a cartel in critical minerals.
Aimed at securing a new supply value chain for AI models and semiconductors for Western countries and US allies in Asia, China is likely to square up to the challenge by ramping up its refining capacity and buying more rare earth deposits from friendly countries in need of hard cash like Myanmar, for example.
To date, 25 countries have signed the Pax Silica Declaration (Pax Silica is Latin for Silicon Peace). Asean countries with known deposits of rare earth include Vietnam, Indonesia, Myanmar, Malaysia and Thailand.
These countries have stayed away from the cartel designed to block cheaper Chinese refined components in critical minerals from entering Western markets that depend on the US for advanced military hardware and for everyday commercial electronics, green energy systems, and medical devices, etc.
By restricting supply, the Pax Silica cartel is likely to start a tech war with China that has the world's largest reserves of rare earth - nearly 48 per cent of the global total and controls over 90 per cent of the world's refining and processing capacity.
Incidentally, China's grip over rare earth did not happen by accident, despite US pressure to restrict ASML - Advanced Semiconductor Materials Lithography - a semiconductor company based in the Netherlands.
ASML was prohibited from sharing the advanced chip-making lithography technology with China. However, Chinese scientists succeeded in leapfrogging the hurdle by improving their own photolithography machines.
The US plans to ban any defence product containing Chinese-derived rare earth magnets from entering its markets and those of those who signed the Pax Silica Declaration.
The fear of security breaches from using China-made magnets, for example, was amplified by an incident in the British Royal Navy, which claimed the cameras on its surveillance system drones were sending signals to an IP address in China!
One nation that is assisting Pax Silica is the Philippines, the current Asean Chair. Manila has earmarked a site of over 1,600 hectares in New Clark City as a major manufacturing and data centre in semiconductors, AI hardware, and critical minerals.
Speaking in Manila during a site visit, Jacob Helberg, US Under Secretary for Economic Affairs, reminded the Filipinos that "when 90 per cent of critical inputs come from one country, you do not have a supply chain. You have a hostage chain".
Thus, he called for a solution to break up China's control over the supply value chain in critical minerals. Pax Silica, therefore, is an asymmetric containment strategy.
Since the West cannot match China's raw refining capacity overnight, it is trying to use legal and financial walls to choke off China's access to global markets and raw materials. Thus, the contest for rare earth deposits has also begun in Asean.
B.A. HAMZAH
Former lecturer,
National Defence University Malaysia (UPNM)
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt mulls single tax agency to streamline revenue collection
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is considering streamlining national revenue administration through a unified collection system, including the proposed establishment of a Single Tax Agency (STA).
The proposal to consolidate the tax collection functions of the Customs Department and the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) was discussed at an enforcement and tax compliance meeting in June.
Sources familiar with the matter told Berita Harian that the meeting was attended by representatives from key Finance Ministry agencies, including the Treasury, Customs Department and IRB, as well as the World Bank.
Currently, Customs and the IRB operate under separate administrative, collection and enforcement frameworks.
The proposed integration could significantly reshape the country's revenue administration by reducing overlapping functions, improving collection efficiency, lowering administrative costs and easing taxpayers' compliance burden.
"The proposal to establish the STA was put forward by the World Bank and discussed at the meeting of national revenue agencies. However, it remains under consideration, and no final decision has been made on restructuring the functions of the two agencies.
"The proposal is being reviewed by the Finance Ministry. Initial discussions have taken place and, if agreed to by the ministry and approved by the relevant authorities, implementation will proceed," a source said.
The source said no timeline had been set for a final decision.
The World Bank, in its Malaysia Economic Monitor June 2015 — Transforming Urban Transport report, had highlighted the need to streamline national revenue administration.
A Berita Harian review found that the World Bank had previously highlighted the need to streamline Malaysia's revenue administration in its Malaysia Economic Monitor June 2015 — Transforming Urban Transport report.
The report said coordinating revenue collection through a single window, even without creating a single agency, could minimise operational overlaps and administrative costs while reducing compliance costs for businesses.
It said a more integrated approach would improve revenue management by eliminating duplicated functions and simplifying procedures for taxpayers.
The report also noted that a more uniform administrative structure would benefit businesses by reducing the time and resources required to meet tax compliance requirements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court dismisses Indira Gandhi's RM100mil suit despite finding gaps in police evidence
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today dismissed kindergarten teacher M. Indira Gandhi's appeal to reinstate her RM100 million suit against the police and government over their alleged failure to locate her daughter, Prasana Diksa.
Despite this dismissal, a three-member bench chaired by Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan found material deficiencies in police evidence regarding their efforts to execute an arrest warrant against her former husband, K. Pathmanathan, also known as Muhammad Riduan Abdullah.
Other members of the bench were Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid.
Pathmanathan is reported to have taken Prasana away 17 years ago after unilaterally converting all three of their children to Islam in 2009. Prasana was 11 months old at the time.
Faizah, who read the unanimous decision, said the evidence did not establish that any particular omission by the police would have likely resulted in Pathmanathan's arrest or Prasana Diksa's recovery.
She said the appellant had to show that the respondents' failure directly caused her loss, and that the loss would probably have been avoided had necessary action been taken.
The court ruled that private law damages cannot be awarded simply for administrative shortcomings.
"Private law damages compensate for loss caused by an actionable wrong. They are not a freestanding response to unsatisfactory administrative performance.
"The respondents did not cause the original taking or the initial separation," she said.
Faizah said immigration records showed Pathmanathan's last recorded official departure from the country was on March 19, 2014, but there was no admissible evidence establishing when or where he had subsequently returned.
"It remained possible that he returned by an unrecorded route or was later present in the country, but no admissible evidence established when or where that occurred.
"Possibility alone could not satisfy the balance of probability," she said.
The appellate court nevertheless found material deficiencies in the police's evidence concerning their efforts to execute the warrant against Pathmanathan.
"No contemporaneous command or direction issued by the then inspector-general of police (IGP) within the stipulated seven days was produced.
"Former IGP Tan Sri Hamid Bador accepted that the delay in issuing the nationwide directive was slow, indeed very slow," she said.
The court also cited shortcomings in evidence relating to the Special Task Force on Organised Crime (STAFOC), noting an absence of contemporaneous documents detailing instructions, actions taken, and results.
However, the court noted that weaknesses in police evidence did not prove the entire investigation was false or a sham.
"We would also like to make it clear that nothing in these grounds should be understood as conferring a general immunity upon the police, or as suggesting that a failure to obey and execute lawful orders and warrants of the courts is legally inconsequential," she said.
Indira filed the suit on Oct 28, 2020, naming Hamid, the police, the Home Ministry and the government as defendants.
The suit stems from her long-running effort to locate Prasana, who was taken by Pathmanathan in March 2009.
The Ipoh High Court had granted Indira custody, care and control of her three children on March 11, 2010, and ordered Pathmanathan to immediately deliver Prasana to her.
On May 30, 2014, the High Court ordered Pathmanathan to be imprisoned until he purged his contempt by delivering Prasana to Indira.
On April 29, 2016, the Federal Court ruled that the then IGP could not refuse to direct police officers to execute the warrant of committal against Pathmanathan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eight including influencer remanded over traffic stopped for race
Article:
KULAI: A motorsports influencer was among eight suspects remanded for four days from today over a viral video showing traffic on the Second Link Expressway being stopped for an illegal race.
The detention order, which runs until Thursday, was issued by Magistrate R. Salini following a police application under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
The suspects, aged between 26 and 45, are being investigated under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
The police truck carrying the suspects arrived at the Kulai Magistrates' Court at about 8.30am today.
[[nid:1517591]]
All the men wore face masks, while two, including the influencer, wore hoodies.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab. Rahaman Arsad said
all eight were arrested
by detectives from the Kulai Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at 11.54am yesterday.
A
33-second clip
showed two motorcyclists racing illegally on the expressway at 7am on Saturday between Km33 near the Senai Utara toll exit and Km31 near the Johor Premium Outlet exit.
Several men had stopped traffic on the expressway to allow the illegal race to proceed.
The footage also showed the group setting off firecrackers to celebrate the end of the race, while several others, including the influencer, were seen on the road shoulder afterwards.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: 10 areas in four states record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ten areas in four states recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today, with Serian, Sarawak, recording the highest reading, nearing the very unhealthy level.
According to data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Sarawak was the worst-affected state, with five areas recording readings above 100, including the Serian district police headquarters (IPD), which recorded an API reading of 194.
Other areas in the state that recorded unhealthy air quality were Kuching (176), Samarahan (172), Sri Aman (158) and Bintulu (125).
The other five areas recording unhealthy API levels were Johan Setia (160) and Kuala Selangor (101) in Selangor; Sungai Petani (155) and Alor Setar (152) in Kedah; and Minden in Penang (130).
A further 58 areas nationwide recorded moderate air quality.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 hazardous.
API data is released hourly based on readings recorded at 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DBKL cracks down on unlicensed entertainment outlets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has cracked down on several entertainment outlets across the capital for operating without a valid license.
During a special operation conducted yesterday, DBKL targeted foreign-operated establishments and business premises that failed to comply with food establishment licensing conditions.
The operation was carried out around the Kepong, Seputeh, and Bukit Bintang parliamentary constituencies.
According to a statement, eight compound notices were issued under the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974, the Licensing of Trades, Businesses and Industries (WPKL) By-Laws 2016, the Licensing of Food Establishments (WPKL) By-Laws 2016, and the Advertisement (WP) By-Laws 1982.
"Three offence notices were also issued to premises operating entertainment without a license.
"In addition, three seizures of entertainment-related items and one immediate closure of premises were executed," the statement read.
DBKL said enforcement operations will continue to ensure business and entertainment premises in Kuala Lumpur comply with the law to maintain public order and community well-being.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PA Resources's jumped 10pct following stellar earnings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PA Resources Bhd's shares rose nearly 10 per cent on Monday morning following a surge in its net profit for the fourth quarter.
Its shares climbed 9.5 per cent to 23 sen in early trade, from 21 sen closing price last Friday, before settling at 22.5 sen at 10.30am. The stock saw more than 22 million shares traded at the time of writing.
The counter rose one sen to open at 22 sen.
Year-to-date, the stock has risen 55.17 per cent.
PA Resources's earnings more than tripled to RM18 million in the fourth quarter ended June 30, 2026 from RM9 million a year earlier lifted by higher sales volume from its extrusion and fabrication business.
For the full year, its earnings climbed 10.8 per cent to RM31 million while revenue rose almost 20 per cent to RM648.6 million from RM541 million last year.
The company declared an interim dividend of 0.5 sen per share, amounting to RM7.5 million and is payable on Oct 31.

Title: Gen Z-inspired songs to feature in National Day celebration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: This year's National Day celebration will feature Gen Z-inspired songs and performances alongside traditional elements as part of a human graphic presentation involving 1,500 school students.
Education Ministry Sports, Co-curriculum and Arts Division director Ithnin Mahadi said the presentation would feature 16 songs spanning current Gen Z music, traditional songs and other genres.
"This year, there are three differences. The first is the song genres, with 16 songs featuring a combination of current Gen Z songs, traditional songs and others.
"We have also incorporated various equipment into the performance, including kompang and trampolines," he said.
He was speaking after the handover ceremony for sponsorship contributions from strategic partners to Human Graphics participants in conjunction with the 2026 National Day celebration here today.
Ithnin said the new elements were expected to give this year's performance a different feel compared with last year's celebration.
He said the 1,500 students involved were from 36 schools under the Selangor Education Department.
The students began preparations in July, initially training separately at their respective schools before coming together for rehearsals at the celebration venue.
"These are the final weeks before National Day, when they will move to the site.
"We will conduct full rehearsals involving all 16 songs to be performed," he said.
Ithnin said organising the human graphic presentation was a major undertaking, particularly in ensuring the welfare, transportation and meals of students during the months of preparation.
He said moving students from 36 schools also involved significant costs, but expressed appreciation to the Communications Ministry for its continued support.
Ithnin, who has been involved in the human graphic presentation since 2021, said the students' welfare remained a priority throughout the preparations.
On preparations for hot weather, he said the students had largely trained indoors before moving to the venue during the final days.
"We start as early as possible to avoid exposing them to the heat. For example, today they will rest at around 11am," he said.
He added that the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Kuala Lumpur remained at a good level today.
The number of students involved this year is lower than last year's 2,000, with 1,500 allocated for the human graphic presentation.
Ithnin said the students involved would generally change from year to year as part of the annual preparations.

Title: Genting privatisation hinges on Resorts World New York turnaround
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The prospect of Genting Bhd making another bid to privatise Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) is likely to depend on whether the turnaround at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) gains enough traction to justify taking the casino operator private, CGS International Securities Malaysia said.
The renewed speculation comes after Genting retained a 73.88 per cent stake in GENM following the expiry of its unconditional mandatory takeover offer in December 2025. The group last bought GENM shares from the open market on April 2, 2026.
"In October 2025, when it launched the mandatory takeover offer of GENM at RM2.35 a share, it said it did not intend to keep the listing status of GENM," said CGS International analyst Chong Tjen-San.
He said a fresh attempt is not imminent, as the success of RWNYC's commercial casino operations remains at an early stage and the business continues to require significant funding.
"In our view, privatisation will largely depend on how convincing the turnaround turns out to be at GENM and in particular Resorts World New York, which looks promising so far but this is still an early day," Chong said in a note.
RWNYC began commercial casino operations in April 2026 and is viewed as GENM's key long-term growth driver. However, Chong believes the operation will continue to weigh on earnings in the near term as it ramps up.
The funding burden also remains a key consideration, he said. Genting recently refinanced a US$1.5 billion bond due in January 2027 by issuing US$1.25 billion of new subordinated perpetual guaranteed notes at a higher interest rate, a move that increases financing costs while preserving liquidity.
Against this backdrop, Chong maintained a "Hold" recommendation on Genting and cut its earnings forecasts for FY26 to FY28 by between 9.0 per cent and 13 per cent.
It also lowered its sum-of-parts target price to RM2.45, reflecting revised valuations for GENM and Genting Plantations Bhd, while applying a 20 per cent holding company discount.
The cautious stance reflects a lack of near-term catalysts, with both GENM and Genting Singapore Ltd (GENS) continuing to underperform expectations.
Chong said downside risks include weaker crude palm oil prices and softer tourist arrivals across Genting's key markets.
Potential upside catalysts include regulatory approval in the United Kingdom for TauRx Pharmaceuticals' Alzheimer's treatment, in which Genting owns a 20 per cent associate stake, as well as a stronger-than-expected recovery at Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NexG plunged 17pct after govt said not buying DTSB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: NexG Bhd shares fell sharply in early trade today after the government said it would not take over Datasonic Technologies Sdn Bhd (DTSB).
The counter opened at 29.5 sen, down 2.5 sen or 7.8 per cent from Friday's close of 32 sen, before falling as much as 5.5 sen or 17.2 per cent to 26.5 sen.
At 10.42am, NexG was trading at 27.5 sen, down 4.5 sen or 14.1 per cent, giving the company a market capitalisation of about RM1 billion.
More than 49.65 million shares changed hands, making NexG the most actively traded counter on Bursa Malaysia.
Meanwhile, its associate NexG Bina Bhd, formerly known as Classita Holdings Bhd, was flat at three sen, giving it a market capitalisation of RM36.98 million.
MMAG Holdings Bhd, in which NexG holds a 9.48 per cent stake, fell half-a-sen or 17 per cent to 2.5 sen, valuing the company at RM58 million.
The sharp decline came after the National Security Council (NSC) on Saturday said the government would not take over DTSB, following recent media reports about a proposed acquisition.
The statement follows reports that the government was considering acquiring DTSB after requesting an indicative price for a possible takeover.
NexG had said its preliminary internal assessment valued DTSB at RM7.5 billion, while stressing that the figure was not an independent valuation, agreed transaction value or firm offer.
DTSB remains a key contributor to NexG's business, with the unit holding several government contracts linked to identity documents.
As of July, DTSB had a RM1.73 billion contract to supply passport booklets and polycarbonate biodata pages to the Immigration Department for the period from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2032.
It also holds a RM732.72 million contract to supply raw cards and consumables to the National Registration Department over the same period.

Title: Genting earnings seen surging on plantations, casino recovery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd has raised its 2026 and 2027 (FY26/FY27) core net profit forecasts for Genting Bhd by 14 per cent and 4.0 per cent respectively, driven largely by a brighter earnings outlook for Genting Plantations Bhd (GENP).
The research house expects Genting's core net profit to rebound 212 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in FY26, supported by narrower losses at Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV) and robust plantation earnings, partly offset by weaker contributions from Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) and Genting Singapore Ltd (GENS).
For FY27, CIMB projects a further 63 per cent increase in core net profit, driven by earnings growth at GENM as Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) scales up its operations, alongside continued improvement at RWLV.
Despite the higher earnings forecasts, CIMB Securities cut its sum-of-parts target price for Genting by 6.0 per cent to RM2.30, citing a higher risk-free rate following the rise in Malaysia's 10-year government bond yield and higher net debt at RWLV by end-2026.
The impact was partly offset by a higher fair value for GENP of RM6.40 a share.
"We continue to ascribe zero equity value to RWLV, as we expect it to be loss-making in the near-to-medium term," CIMB Securities analyst Choong Chen Foong said in a note.
He said upside risks include stronger-than-expected earnings from GENS and GENM, while key downside risks centre on RWLV taking longer than anticipated to achieve sustainable profitability.
Within the group, he said CIMB Securities favours GENM as the "purest play" on the expansion of RWNYC's commercial casino business.
GENM's core net profit fell 46 per cent YoY to RM132 million in Q2 FY26, although it more than doubled from the previous quarter.
The sharp annual decline was mainly due to higher depreciation and net interest expenses associated with the newly launched commercial casino operations at RWNYC, which opened on April 28, 2026.
Underlying operations remained resilient, with GENM's EBITDA rising 1.0 per cent YoY and 35 per cent QoQ, driven by Resorts World Genting, where cost controls and an improved VIP win rate supported earnings.
The US segment also began contributing following RWNYC's commercial launch.
CIMB expects GENM's FY26 core earnings per share to halve, weighed down by lower-than-expected earnings from RWNYC as the new casino operation continues to scale up.
GENS delivered a mixed performance, with EBITDA rising 12 per cent YoY and 18 per cent QoQ, while core net profit fell 4.0 per cent YoY to S$94 million (RM294 million).
The decline reflected higher depreciation charges from ongoing asset enhancement works and lower interest income. However, core net profit rebounded 35 per cent QoQ from a weak first quarter, helped by a sharp reduction in operating expenses.
Gaming revenue was broadly flat YoY and declined 1.0 per cent QoQ, while non-gaming revenue grew 3.0 per cent YoY but fell 10 per cent QoQ, despite support from new attractions including the Singapore Oceanarium and WEAVE.
CIMB expects GENS' FY26 core net profit to decline 12 per cent YoY, mainly due to softer gaming revenue and higher costs.
GENP was the standout performer, with core net profit surging 2.7 times YoY and 2.3 times QoQ to RM140 million.
The stronger performance was driven by a 12 per cent increase in fresh fruit bunches output, a 2.0 per cent rise in palm kernel prices and a 15 per cent YoY decline in crude palm oil production costs.
CIMB raised its GENP earnings forecasts for FY26 and FY27 by 18 per cent, incorporating a RM50-per-tonne increase in its CPO price assumptions and raising its FY26 FFB growth forecast to 7.0 per cent from 4.0 per cent previously.
"We now forecast GENP's full-year 2026 core net profit to grow 22 per cent YoY," CIMB said.
At RWLV, EBITDA fell 52 per cent QoQ to US$97 million (RM388 million), following an exceptionally strong start to the year, although it remained 33 per cent above Q2 FY25.
Revenue rose 1.0 per cent YoY but declined 13 per cent QoQ, supported by higher convention attendance following the late-2025 expansion of the Las Vegas Convention Center.
Hotel occupancy improved to 88 per cent from 80.2 per cent a year earlier, while average daily rates increased 3.0 per cent.
CIMB expects RWLV's net loss to narrow 35 per cent YoY in FY26.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dollar trading near multi-month lows, restrained by debt nerves
Article:
SINGAPORE: A wavering dollar teetered near multi-month lows on Monday in a market unsettled by the US Treasury's promise to buy back more long bonds, while traders awaited details of sanctions on Iran and on policy speeches this week in the US and Japan.
The Canadian dollar slipped 0.2 per cent in early trade, to CUS$1.3798 per dollar, after trade talks with the US collapsed and Washington imposed 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian goods, with Canada retaliating in kind.
The Australian and New Zealand dollars traded just shy of three-month highs at US$0.7171 and US$0.5979 respectively.
The euro was comfortably above US$1.16 at US$1.1685 while the yen kept to the strong side of 159 per dollar.
Friday data showing the strongest US services growth in nearly two years in August held off dollar sellers in steady early trade.
The dollar logged its largest weekly drop against bitcoin in nearly three-and-a-half years on Sunday and it's been sliding sharply on gold over revived fears the currency will suffer if the US tries to hold down yields.
Long-end yields have been climbing globally on a combination of a solid economic growth outlook, rising inflation expectations and nerves about ballooning sovereign debts.
Last week, after 30-year yields hit almost two-decade highs, the US Treasury announced it would double buybacks at the long end to US$4 billion per operation.
The size is paltry in a market worth US$32 trillion but the interventionist signal spooked traders and hit the dollar.
"The US Treasury's attempts to artificially hold down long-term bond yields appears to be reigniting the US$US debasement trade," said Shane Oliver, head of investment strategy at Australian financial services firm AMP.
The mood was keeping Australian dollar above 71 cents, he said.
Sterling was firm at US$1.3650 in morning trade and the yuan, which notched an eighth straight weekly rise last week, hovered near a 3/1-2 year high at 6.7222 per dollar.
SANCTIONS AND WARSH
Later on Monday, at 1800 GMT, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference after threatening "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran, with markets focused on whether he will target China.
Iran's foreign minister has dismissed the threat of new US sanctions as a sign of desperation.
Market participants will also be hoping for some clarity on the outlook for US interest rates when Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday.
He is also sure to face questions about Treasury's buybacks.
"Any comments on the balance sheet, duration supply, or term premium could move the long end more than the data itself. That said, given Warsh's typically restrained style, we aren't holding our breath," said BNY strategist Geoff Yu.
A Thursday appearance by Bank of Japan deputy governor Ryozo Himino will also be closely watched as a prelude to next month's policy meeting. In particular, investors will be looking to see if he pushes back on a shift in market pricing to see a faster pace of hikes.
"Himino may signal the BOJ is moving closer to another interest rate hike," said Commonwealth Bank of Australia strategist Joe Capurso.
"However, any hawkish comments are likely to exert only modest downward pressure on USD/JPY. Developments in the US bond market area are a more important driver of USD/JPY."

Title: Solehah to challenge IIUM dismissal in Industrial Court
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Academic Dr Solehah Yaacob will challenge the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) over its decision to terminate her services by taking the matter to the Industrial Court.
Solehah said she had rejected IIUM's offer of compensation equivalent to six months' salary following her dismissal.
"I was dismissed within 24 hours and was not given the opportunity to appeal.
"IIUM wanted to pay me compensation equivalent to six months' salary, but I rejected it," she told FMT.
IIUM had previously confirmed that
Solehah's service
as an academic staff member ended on April 27.
In a statement, IIUM's Office for Communication, Advocacy and Promotion for Change (OCAP) said Solehah no longer held the position of professor at the university or represented IIUM in any capacity.
The university also said she was no longer permitted to use any title, position or form of official association with IIUM, including in social media content, publicity materials or other forms of dissemination, whether directly or indirectly.
Solehah claimed that UIAM had acted unprofessionally in terminating her services, particularly as she had received the Malaysia Research Assessment (MyRA) award from the Higher Education Ministry a day earlier.
MyRA, introduced in 2006, is an evaluation framework used to assess the research performance of universities nationwide.
Solehah had previously attracted public attention over several controversial views, including those concerning Malay history and civilisation.
Among her
reported views
was a claim that ancient Romans had learned shipbuilding technology from people in the Malay Archipelago.
IIUM had previously said the clarification on Solehah's employment status was issued to help avoid any misunderstanding and uphold the integrity and academic standing of the university.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gold hits over 3-month high ahead of US inflation data, Fed chair speech
Article:
BENGALURU: Gold prices hit their highest levels in more than three months on Monday as a subdued dollar lent support, while focus shifted to key US inflation data and a speech later this week by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh.
Spot gold was up 0.5 per cent at US$4,627.42 per ounce, as of 0155 GMT, after hitting its highest level since May 15 earlier in the session. Prices gained more than five per cent last week.
US gold futures edged 0.1 per cent higher to US$4,683.80.
A wavering dollar teetered near multi-month lows in a market unsettled by the US Treasury's promise to buy back more long bonds. A weaker US dollar makes greenback-priced bullion more affordable for holders of other currencies.
Gold is looking spritely to start the week and has stepped back into bid mode and is taking its cues primarily from the softer dollar and focusing more on what higher yields may be signaling about underlying economic strains and policy uncertainty, said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.
The July Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index data and Fed Chair Warsh's speech at the Jackson Hole symposium this week will be watched for fresh clues on the US interest rate outlook.
"Traders will be listening closely for any shift in tone on the policy path and how it sits with recent bond-market developments. A balanced or cautious tone that leaves room for flexibility would likely keep the door open for gold to extend its gains," Waterer added.
On the geopolitical front, the US threatened Iran with what it called "the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled" as it prepared to roll out economic sanctions that target Iran's trade partners. Oil prices slipped more than US$1 a barrel as investors took profits ahead of the expected announcement.
Among other metals, spot silver fell 0.3 per cent to US$68.76 per ounce. Platinum lost 0.5 per cent to US$1,868.03 while palladium was down 0.3 per cent at US$1,345.87.

Title: Oil falls ahead of US announcement on new Iran sanctions
Article:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices slipped more than US$1 a barrel on Monday as investors took profits ahead of an expected announcement from Washington about imposing more sanctions on Iran that may further disrupt supplies from the Middle East.
Brent crude futures fell US$1.22, or 1.29 per cent, to US$93.17 by 0035 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$85.86 a barrel, down US$1.20, or 1.38 per cent.
Both contracts posted their second weekly gains last week, up more than five per cent, as peace talks between the US and Iran hit a stalemate, capping oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz where a fifth of the world's supply used to transit.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, set to hold a press conference at 2pm EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday, has threatened to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran. President Donald Trump has also threatened to impose sanctions on Iran's trading partners.
"It is unclear whether US policy to economically isolate Iran will prove effective," Vivek Dhar, a commodities analyst at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, wrote in a note.
"But if the US measures do work as intended, Iran's ability to respond via increased violence becomes a growing risk for energy markets to consider." Iran has condemned US plans to announce new sanctions even as President Masoud Pezeshkian called for a diplomatic solution.
"The more pragmatic members of the Iranian leadership would prefer to de-escalate but the hardliners would probably prefer to fight to the bitter end," IG markets analyst Tony Sycamore said.
"I think by the end of this week we will have a good idea which side of the Iranian leadership has the upper hand." Offers of Iranian crude to Chinese buyers have declined and prices have jumped as the US blockade has cut Tehran's shipments, according to trade sources. However, Iran has granted permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the Strait following repeated requests from Baghdad, Iran's state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday.

Title: Shares flat in Asia before Iran sanctions news, Nvidia results
Article:
SYDNEY: Share markets were flat in Asia on Monday and oil prices eased as investors awaited details of threatened US sanctions on Iran due later in the session, while the Canadian dollar dipped as a trade war loomed with its southern neighbour.
The entire tech sector is holding its breath for Nvidia's results on Wednesday; investors are aware how hard it will be for the chip maker to meet stratospheric expectations.
Analysts are generally looking for quarterly revenue to almost double to around US$92 billion, with full-year earnings guidance seen in a range of US$103 billion to US$105 billion.
Market participants will also be hoping for some clarity on the outlook for US interest rates when Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday, though his well-known aversion to forward guidance could lead to disappointment.
"There are several reasons to expect to be underwhelmed," said Bruce Kasman, chief economist at JPMorgan, noting that past chairs have not wanted to front-run Fed decisions at the event.
"Warsh will rather likely focus on aspects of his 'regime change' agenda," Kasman added. "As the Fed has already been moving toward shrinking the balance sheet, and the committee gave the balance sheet some attention in the July minutes, that might be the most likely topic for him to expound upon."
Markets imply around a 40 per cent chance that the Fed will raise interest rates when it meets on September 16 and are fully priced for a move by December.
The odds could change depending on what US inflation figures show this week, with median forecasts for core inflation expected to hold at 3.3 per cent in July.
Warsh is sure to face questions about Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's surprise announcement last week of at least a doubling in bond buybacks, aimed at restraining a rise in yields that was tightening financial conditions in the economy.
His efforts have had little success so far, with 30-year yields back up at 5.2760 per cent, not far from the recent 19-year peak of 5.3371 per cent.
Higher yields make debt more attractive compared to equities while lifting the discount applied to future earnings, highlighting the stretched nature of some valuations.
SANCTIONS AND TRADE WARS
Bessent is due to hold a news conference later on Monday to outline sanctions on Iran, which has shown no sign of relinquishing its control over the vital Strait of Hormuz.
Brent slipped 1.0 per cent to US$93.43 ahead of the announcement, though that followed gains of 6.6 per cent last week. US crude eased 1.1 per cent to US$86.14 a barrel.
Equity markets were quiet in early trade, with the Nikkei near flat after having fallen almost 4 per cent last week. South Korean shares eased 0.8 per cent, while Taiwan dipped 0.5 per cent.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan eased 0.2 per cent.
In Europe, EURO STOXX 50 futures, DAX futures and FTSE futures were all little changed. On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq futures were a fraction lower.
In currency markets, the dollar added 0.1 per cent against its Canadian counterpart to 1.3784 after Prime Minister Mark Carney said his country would respond to US tariffs with levies of its own as trade talks broke down.
Canada will impose tariffs on US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics, along with some products that the US previously targeted in Canada.
The dollar was on the defensive elsewhere after having lost 0.8 per cent last week against a basket of currencies at 96.832. The euro held at US$1.1675 after rising 0.9 per cent last week, while the dollar was flat at 159.00 yen.
The dollar has been undermined as investors fret that growing US debt and policy uncertainties will erode the purchasing power of the currency, driving demand for scarcer assets including gold.
The yellow metal firmed 0.4 per cent to US$4,623 an ounce, having climbed more than 14 per cent for the month so far. If it holds this gain for all of August, it would be the biggest monthly rise on record. (

Title: Japan's Nikkei wavers as AI stocks weigh ahead of Nvidia earnings
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's Nikkei share average moved between small gains and losses on Monday, with artificial intelligence-related shares under pressure ahead of Nvidia earnings later in the week.
The market was also weighed down by inflation worries amid continued uncertainty in the Middle East, with investors and analysts expecting the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates at its next policy meeting in September.
Japanese government bond yields ticked higher in morning trading.
The Nikkei was 0.2 per cent higher at 65,900.95 at 0156 GMT, after oscillating between gains of as much as 0.4 per cent and losses of 0.5 per cent.
Most AI-related shares, which tend to be heavily weighted on the Nikkei, declined, with Fujikura losing 3.5 per cent and SoftBank Group slipping 3.3 per cent
Chip-making tool manufacturers outperformed, though, with Tokyo Electron rising 2.1 per cent.
The broader Topix inched up 0.1 per cent.
Nvidia has notified some of its largest customers that AI server prices will rise by more than 15 per cent amid soaring memory costs, Bloomberg reported on Saturday. The company announces financial results on Wednesday.
"We view the concerns over the profitability of semiconductor-related companies — led by Nvidia — as little more than a pretext or trigger for selling" following "a significant build-up of open positions in margin trading recently", said Wataru Akiyama, an equities strategist at Nomura Securities.
"I think it is fair to say that the outlook for earnings growth in AI and semiconductor-related stocks has not changed."
At the same time, with bond yields rising as a result of building inflation worries, "it does not appear that the Japanese stock market is currently in a position to sustain an upward trend", he added.
