Title: FMM dismisses MTUC’s RM3,100 minimum wage proposal as unrealistic for businesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) has rejected a proposal by the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) to raise the national minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM3,100, cautioning that an 82.4 per cent surge is detached from prevailing economic realities.
FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said that while the federation supports higher wages as Malaysia strives for high-income status, an abrupt RM1,400 increase in a single revision remains unprecedented. Such an adjustment, he stressed, cannot occur without weighing productivity gains, employer affordability, export competitiveness, inflation, and the ripple effects across entire company pay scales.
The pushback follows remarks on Sunday by MTUC secretary-general Kamarul Baharin Mansor, who framed RM3,100 as a necessary "living wage" benchmark. Kamarul argued against views that statutory reviews should not automatically trigger rate hikes, calling that position dismissive of low-income earners stuck at the baseline. He noted that the RM3,100 threshold reflects escalating costs for food, housing, and transport, citing instances of decade-long employees still earning RM1,700 due to rigid pay structures.
Under the National Wages Consultative Council (NWCC) Act, the next mandatory statutory wage review is slated for February 2027. The current RM1,700 threshold took effect in February 2025 and became mandatory across all employer categories in August 2025.
FMM pointed out that statutory minimum wage revisions since 2013 have always been gradual, rising incrementally from RM900 and RM800 in 2013 to RM1,700 in 2025. With enterprises still adapting to the latest rate, the federation cautioned that raising the baseline to RM3,100 would place it uncomfortably close to Malaysia's formal sector median wage of RM3,167 recorded in December 2025.
Such wage compression would compel employers to lift pay scales for supervisors, technicians, and skilled staff to maintain internal pay differentials, driving total operational payrolls far beyond the direct cost of minimum-wage adjustments. FMM warned this burden would fall hardest on small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and labour-intensive manufacturers, raising the risk of business closures, operational relocations, and reduced entry-level hiring.
Highlighting regional dynamics, FMM warned that a RM3,100 threshold would widen the gap between Malaysia and competing Asean manufacturing hubs. Minimum monthly wages currently range from roughly RM570 to RM820 in Vietnam, RM1,080 to RM1,280 in Thailand, RM560 to RM1,450 across Indonesian provinces, and around RM1,300 in Metro Manila. Widening this divide without equal productivity gains risks dampening Malaysia's industrial edge.
FMM urged that all wage revisions remain anchored within the tripartite NWCC framework, relying on empirical data including productivity indices, cost of living, sector-specific health, and employer balance sheets. Any upcoming adjustment must remain moderate, predictable, and paired with ample notice.
The federation also called on the government to widen fiscal support for SMEs in Budget 2027 through competitive tax structures and expanded incentives for automation, digitalisation, and upskilling to drive a "virtuous cycle" of sustainable wage growth.
"The distinction between a statutory minimum wage, which provides a basic wage floor, and the broader aspiration for a living wage must be properly recognised," Lee said, adding that the sustainable path to better pay runs through productivity, skills and business growth rather than a single large increase in the statutory floor.

Title: E-hailing driver charged with attempted murder after setting woman on fire in Kepong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — An e-hailing driver has claimed trial at the Sessions Court here to an attempted murder charge after allegedly dousing a 62-year-old woman in petrol and setting her ablaze in Kepong earlier this month.
Ang Kam Tong, 58, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before Judge Surita Budin,
FMT
reported.
Ang is accused of attempting to murder Gan Siew Teen by dousing her with fuel and setting her on fire, inflicting severe injuries. The alleged attack took place at a betting outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong, Sentul, at around 7.51am on August 9.
The offence, framed under Section 307 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum prison term of 20 years upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Shakila Shariff objected to bail, telling the court that Ang had attempted to evade arrest. She also urged the bench to consider the severity of the victim's condition, noting that Gan sustained third-degree burns.
In pleading for bail, defence counsel Lee Keng Fatt argued that his client is presumed innocent until proven guilty. He told the court that Ang is unmarried, works as an e-hailing driver with no fixed income, and that his siblings were ready to post bail on his behalf.
Surita granted bail at RM15,000 with one surety and fixed September 25 for case mention.

Title: Court of Appeal dismisses Indira Gandhi’s RM100m suit despite flagging police shortcomings
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — The Court of Appeal today dismissed Hindu mother M. Indira Gandhi’s appeal to reinstate her RM100 million lawsuit against the police and the Malaysian government over their failure to track down her youngest daughter, Prasana Diksa.
While dismissing the appeal, a three-member bench chaired by Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan highlighted material deficiencies in police records concerning efforts to execute an arrest warrant against her fugitive former husband, K. Pathmanathan, also known as Muhammad Riduan Abdullah,
NST
reported.
Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid also sat on the bench.
Delivering the unanimous decision, Faizah ruled that the available evidence failed to establish that any specific police omission directly prevented Pathmanathan’s arrest or the recovery of Prasana.
The appellate court held that the appellant was required to prove that the respondents’ inaction directly caused her loss, and that such loss would have likely been averted had proper measures been carried out.
The court maintained that private law damages cannot be granted simply to penalise administrative inadequacies.
“Private law damages compensate for loss caused by an actionable wrong. They are not a freestanding response to unsatisfactory administrative performance.
“The respondents did not cause the original taking or the initial separation,” Faizah said.
Turning to immigration records, Faizah pointed out that Pathmanathan’s last documented departure from Malaysia occurred on March 19, 2014, with no admissible records indicating if or when he re-entered the country.
“It remained possible that he returned by an unrecorded route or was later present in the country, but no admissible evidence established when or where that occurred.
“Possibility alone could not satisfy the balance of probability,” she said.
Even so, the appellate judges took issue with critical gaps in the evidence presented by the police regarding their execution of the arrest warrant.
“No contemporaneous command or direction issued by the then inspector-general of police (IGP) within the stipulated seven days was produced.
“Former IGP Tan Sri Hamid Bador accepted that the delay in issuing the nationwide directive was slow, indeed very slow,” Faizah noted.
The bench also flagged evidentiary gaps involving the now-disbanded Special Task Force on Organised Crime (STAFOC), citing a total lack of contemporaneous documentation detailing specific instructions, actions taken, and tangible results.
However, the judges clarified that procedural weaknesses in police documentation do not automatically render the entire investigation fabricated.
“We would also like to make it clear that nothing in these grounds should be understood as conferring a general immunity upon the police, or as suggesting that a failure to obey and execute lawful orders and warrants of the courts is legally inconsequential,” Faizah added.
Indira filed the suit on October 28, 2020, naming Abdul Hamid, the Royal Malaysia Police, the Home Ministry, and the government as respondents.
The lawsuit marked another chapter in Indira’s protracted, 17-year battle to find Prasana, who was taken by Pathmanathan in March 2009 after he unilaterally converted their three children to Islam. Prasana was only 11 months old at the time.
The Ipoh High Court granted Indira full custody, care, and control of the children on March 11, 2010, ordering Pathmanathan to surrender Prasana immediately.
On May 30, 2014, the High Court issued a committal order to imprison Pathmanathan until he purged his contempt by returning the child. The Federal Court subsequently ruled on April 29, 2016, that the IGP could not refuse to direct police officers to execute the committal warrant against him.

Title: Sarawak leads haze misery as Serian hits 194, unhealthy API spreads to Selangor, Kedah, Penang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Ten areas in four states recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today, with Serian, Sarawak recording the highest reading, nearing the very unhealthy level.
According to data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Sarawak was the worst-affected state, with five areas recording readings above 100, including the Serian district police headquarters (IPD), which recorded an API reading of 194.
Other areas in the state that recorded unhealthy air quality were Kuching (176), Samarahan (172), Sri Aman (158) and Bintulu (125).
The other five areas recording unhealthy API levels were Johan Setia (160) and Kuala Selangor (101) in Selangor; Sungai Petani (155) and Alor Setar (152) in Kedah; and Minden in Penang (130).
A further 58 areas nationwide recorded moderate air quality.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 hazardous.
API data is released hourly based on readings recorded at 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Three squatter homes razed in Sentul blaze, 26‑year‑old man treated for burn injuries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — A man suffered burns to his body and legs in a fire that destroyed three squatter houses in Jalan Ismail Ghani, Kampung Kasipillay, Sentul, here early this morning.
Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mukhtar said the emergency call was received at 1.15am before teams from Sentul, Hang Tuah and Gombak Selatan Fire and Rescue Stations rushed to the location.
“Upon arrival of the fire brigade at the location, the fire was found to involve three semi-permanent squatter houses with a total area of 4,872 square feet.
“The houses were 100 per cent destroyed,” he said in a statement today.
Ahmad Mukhlis said the victim, a 26-year-old local man, was sent to the Kuala Lumpur Hospital and placed in the Red Zone for further treatment.
The fire was successfully brought under control, while the cause of the incident is still under investigation by JBPM Forensic Unit, he said. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Anwar, Amirudin meet as Pakatan weighs BN pact
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met with Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari over the weekend, with a potential electoral pact with Barisan Nasional for the next Melaka state polls believed to be high on the agenda.
PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil confirmed the meeting took place, though he noted he was not briefed on the specifics.
Speaking to reporters after a National Day human graphic performance sponsorship ceremony in Putrajaya, Fahmi said coalition chiefs have held a flurry of discussions over the past two days,
The Star
reported.
“I understand they met yesterday, but I was not told what was discussed,” he said.
The prospect of a joint PH-BN ticket could mirror their cooperation during the six state elections in 2023.
However, with BN having partnered with Perikatan Nasional in more recent state contests in Negeri Sembilan and Johor, the eventual configuration of alliances in Melaka remains fluid.
Fahmi also referenced Anwar’s address at the PH congress in Melaka on Aug 16, where the PKR president called for reconciliation with veteran figures such as Tian Chua and Dr Xavier Jayakumar while reinforcing internal coalition unity.
Dr Xavier has since confirmed his return to PKR, while Tian Chua has welcomed the overture.
On the BN front, chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has maintained that the coalition will not enter any automatic arrangement with Perikatan, leaving the ultimate decision to Melaka Chief Minister and state Umno-Barisan chief Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang noted on Friday that Perikatan and Barisan were already in discussions over seat allocations in Melaka, though he cautioned that Perikatan is prepared to go its own way should Barisan opt for Pakatan instead.
Injecting fresh urgency into the race, PN chairman and Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar suggested at a PAS fundraiser yesterday that the Melaka polls could take place within two months.
He urged the coalition machinery to treat the 60-day window as a decisive battleground rather than a routine runway, keeping his reasons for the specific timeframe close to his chest.
Speaking alongside Hadi, Ahmad Samsuri affirmed that PN stands ready to join Melaka’s next administration regardless of the eventual political alignment, pledging equitable representation for the state’s diverse communities.

Title: Noise row in Sarawak turns violent as knife attack leaves man wounded outside Bau home
Article:
BAU, Aug 24 — A 40-year-old man sustained injuries to his face and wrist after a dispute over noise-making escalated into a violent attack in front of a house at Kampung Serikin near here last Saturday.
Bau District police chief Supt Mohd Haide A. Rahman said the incident took place at around 1pm, when the complainant became involved in a heated argument with the suspect.
“The confrontation arose from his growing frustration over the suspect’s persistent noise-making in the area.
“What began as a verbal exchange quickly turned physical when the suspect brandished a knife that had been tucked into the back of his waistband and swung the blade towards the victim, hitting his left cheek.
“The victim also sustained a minor laceration to his left wrist while attempting to block the knife during the assault,” he said in a statement.
Mohd Haide said the suspect had been identified and the knife had been seized.
The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt using dangerous weapons or means. — The Borneo Post

Title: Melaka election countdown? Perikatan hints at polls within two months
Article:
AYER KEROH, Aug 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) has teased a tight timeline for the Melaka state election, suggesting the polls could be held in less than two months and putting the coalition’s election machinery on high alert.
PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar warned that a 60-day window should not be mistaken for a long period, but rather viewed as a critical countdown to determine who will govern the state,
NST
reported.
“There is a reason why I mentioned two months, but there is no need to explain it here,” the Terengganu menteri besar said during the PAS Melaka fundaiser last night.
“Do not see 60 days as a long period. Instead, see it as a period that will determine the form of government that will administer Melaka.”
Speaking in the presence of PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang, Ahmad Samsuri, who also serves as a PAS vice-president, vowed that PN is prepared to govern Melaka regardless of the political landscape.
He emphasised that the coalition is committed to securing a role in the state administration to ensure the interests of all communities are protected and treated with equity.
“We have made our commitment in PAS and PN to be part of the administration of Melaka, regardless of who leads the state,” he said.
“We recognise the diversity of communities here and will govern Melaka with that diversity in mind.”
Ahmad Samsuri argued that fairness in governance is the only way to ensure Melaka remains a peaceful and prosperous state, promising that a PN or PN-influenced administration would serve as a model of harmony.
“Everyone’s interests will be considered and protected fairly. This will ensure Melaka becomes an example of a peaceful, prosperous and harmonious state,” he added.

Title: Mr Opposition — The legacy of Tan Chee Khoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — A steady crowd of 150 or so were present at yesterday’s public forum marking 30 years since the death of former opposition leader Dr Tan Chee Khoon.
Jointly organised by Aliran and his youngest daughter Tan Poh Lai, the event at the KLSCAH is one of three subtitled Merdeka, Multiracialism and Dissent, Without Fear or Favour. Subsequent events are to be held on Sept 3 in Ipoh and Sept 5 in Penang.
For the uninitiated, Tan Chee Khoon was the official Leader of the Opposition in the Dewan Rakyat from 1964 to 1969. He was elected to Parliament in 1964 under the Labour Party, 1969 under Gerakan and 1974 under Pekemas.
Poh Lai did a great job of conveying the life story of this exemplary Malaysian who was committed to a multiracial outlook and whose socialism was also tempered by a strong Christian commitment.
Her reflection on the story behind the man was engrossing and touching in turn.
She recounted how he had been blinded in one eye as a 12-year-old following an accident while tapping rubber. She said that the loss of his eye was due to a lack of funds and access to proper medical care, which made him a compassionate and caring physician.
She recalled too how he was drawn into the left-wing struggle and remained steadfast despite many challenges such as the decimation of the Labour Party and the Socialist Front through the detention without trial of numerous leaders ranging from Ahmad Boestamam, Karam Singh, Tan Kai Hee, MK Rajakumar, Syed Husin Ali, Hasnol Hadi and many others.
“Many times, the other side tried to lure him over but he was steadfast and flatly turned down political positions like Deputy Chief Minister because it did not align with his brand of multiracial politics. Even to this day I will never join a party that is based on race, due to the principles he instilled,” said Poh Lai.
Her father had to rebuild on a number of occasions, leaving the Labour Party to form multiracial Gerakan only to see Lim Chong Eu subvert the party’s original left-leaning ethos by steering it into Barisan Nasional in the early 1970s.
Tan then formed Pekemas with Gerakan rebels but was the only one elected to Parliament in 1974 and was forced to step back from politics after suffering the first of two strokes in 1977. He died in 1996 having made his mark as a medical doctor and a prominent columnist with his “Without Fear or Favour” column in The Star.
His son Dr Tan Kee Kwong was Land and Cooperative Development deputy minister from 1999 to 2004 and served four terms in parliament, representing first Gerakan, then PKR. Poh Lai too was active in PKR and has also acted as legal representative for the Orang Asli in land rights dispute cases.
Economist Jomo Kwame Sundaram also spoke at the event and reflected on Tan’s commitment to principles, saying that he came from an era when political leaders could choose to debate ideology and not focus on identity factors like race and religion.
“It was a different time with politics and the debates about different ideas and views of the world going forward. The debates were about a different conception of the nation, and Tan was very much part of it,” he said.
Jomo lamented the suppression of the left-wing political movement in Malaysia, saying that its role has now been overlooked or omitted.

Title: Hadi: Perikatan and BN already in talks for Melaka state election pact
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) have entered negotiations to forge a cooperation pact for the upcoming Melaka state election (PRN).
PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang disclosed that talks between representatives appointed by the central leadership of both coalitions kicked off three days ago,
Sinar Harian
reported.
While acknowledging that discussions are in their infancy, Abdul Hadi noted that the initial momentum has been promising.
“Preparations at the party level have already begun and are ongoing. These discussions will continue to the next stage,” he said during a fundraiser dinner last night.
When questioned on the likelihood of a formal alliance, Abdul Hadi remained cautious but optimistic.
“That is still at an early stage, but even now, it has shown very good progress. The progress of the discussions has been very positive. We are taking inspiration from what was successfully achieved in Johor and Negeri Sembilan,” he added.
Regarding the timing of the polls, Abdul Hadi acknowledged that the date remains unknown, though the groundwork for cooperation is already being laid.
The confirmation follows similar sentiments from PN Chief Whip Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan on Saturday, who said that the two sides are closing in on a mutual understanding.
According to Takiyuddin, while initial feedback from BN has been positive, the finer details of the cooperation, specifically the division of state seats, are yet to be finalised.
Also in attendance at the dinner were PN chairman and PAS vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, and Melaka PAS commissioner Zulkifli Ismail.

Title: Housewife in her 70s tricked by ritual scam in Sibu, police confirm RM317,000 losses
Article:
SIBU, Aug 24 — An elderly housewife lost RM317,000 after she was allegedly duped by a scam syndicate using a modus operandi involving traditional healing and a ritual to ward off misfortune here.
Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the local woman, in her 70s, lodged a police report yesterday over the incident, which occurred on July 19 in the Sibu Market area.
He said the victim was initially approached by an unidentified woman, believed to be a Chinese national based on her accent, who asked for directions to a Chinese traditional medicine shop, allegedly to obtain medicine for her mother-in-law.
“Shortly afterwards, another woman with a similar accent approached the victim and offered to take them to a shop allegedly owned by her relative.
“The victim was then taken in a vehicle before one of the suspects claimed she could read her face and told her that her child would be involved in a serious road accident that day,” he said in a statement.
Abang Zainal Abidin said the suspects then offered a protection ritual and asked the victim to hand over cash and jewellery for the purpose.
He said the victim, who was worried about her child’s safety, believed the claims and handed over the cash and jewellery, resulting in total losses estimated at RM317,000.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
Abang Zainal Abidin advised the public not to easily trust strangers offering traditional treatments or rituals to ward off misfortune in exchange for cash or jewellery.
The public was also urged not to be easily influenced by claims or threats deliberately intended to cause fear and anxiety, prompting them to hand over money or valuables. — Bernama

Title: Record-breaking crowds storm Menara Merdeka 118 for IHH Sky Race
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, August 24 — More than 8,000 athletes stormed the 118 floors of Menara Merdeka 118 over the weekend, as the IHH Sky Race returned for its second year to cement its status as Malaysia’s premier tower running event.
The two-day spectacle drew participants from 78 countries and secured a spot in the Malaysia Book of Records for the Largest Participation in a Tower Running Event. With 7,797 finishers crossing the line, the race comfortably eclipsed last year’s milestone of 5,602.
The competition was fiercest in the men’s category. Japanese tower runner Ryoji Watanabe claimed victory with a blistering time of 15 minutes and 38 seconds. He missed breaking the 2025 course record by a mere second, falling just short of the 15 minutes and 37 seconds mark set by Malaysia’s Soh Wai Ching.
Soh secured second place, conquering the 2,845 steps in 15 minutes and 48 seconds, while Australian Mark Bourne followed in third at 16 minutes and 33 seconds.
“This win was a bittersweet one for me as it was evident that Wai Ching was not in top condition,” said Watanabe, who viewed the Malaysian as his primary rival.
“This tower’s course is quite interesting and not something that I have experienced before, so it took a while to get my bearings. I want to challenge the course again next year, so I will definitely be back.”
IHH Sky Race winner Ryoji Watanabe (right) and runner-up Soh Wai Ching (left) catch their breath after scaling 118 floors in 15 minutes at Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur on August 22, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Despite the loss, Soh found a silver lining in the survival of his record.
“I gave my best today, and while I am disappointed that I could not manage to get the win this year, I am glad that my course record from last year still stands. I will certainly come back next year to improve my time.”
The event also served as a showcase for emerging talent and international dominance. Croatian runner Tea Faber, 37, decimated the Women’s Open record, finishing in 18 minutes and 7 seconds to beat the previous best of 19 minutes and 59 seconds.
Local youth also shone on the day. Fourteen-year-old Adam Amjad clocked 18 minutes and 36 seconds to set a new Junior Boy record, while 12-year-old Rhea Assyifa Rosli crushed the Junior Girl record, finishing in 24 minutes and 15 seconds, far surpassing the previous mark of 32 minutes and 35 seconds.
Race director Jeffrey Ross confirmed that approximately 200 medical personnel were stationed across checkpoints in the world's second tallest building to manage cramps and fainting spells, ensuring all athletes were safely cared for.
“This year’s expanded two-day format allowed us to welcome more participants than ever before, and the response has exceeded our expectations,” said Ross, who is also the managing director of Fresh Events Asia.
“Achieving the Malaysia Book of Records title for Largest Participation in a Tower Running Event is a proud milestone for the team, and a clear sign that The IHH Sky Race has become one of the region’s biggest and most significant tower-running events.”
Beyond the vertical sprint, the event transformed Stadium Merdeka into the Sky Race Village from August 20 to 23. The hub offered a festival atmosphere with live music, interactive games, and a variety of food and beverage stalls.
The race was flagged off on Saturday morning by a distinguished delegation, including IHH Healthcare Malaysia CEO Dr Kamal Amzan, PNB Group Chairman Raja Tan Sri Arshad Raja Tun Uda, PNB Merdeka Ventures CEO Datuk Izwan Ibrahim, and IHH Healthcare Malaysia’s Regional CEO and Corporate Clinical Services Dr Shuba Srinivasan.
Sanctioned by the Malaysian Towerrunning Association (MTA), the event was powered by title partner IHH Healthcare Malaysia, with support from the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC), EBENE, and Oligo.

Title: Amirudin says viral Sukma holiday poster fake, official decision based on medal tally tonight
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 24 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has denied the authenticity of a viral poster announcing a special public holiday to mark the state’s victory at the 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma).
In a post on Threads, Amirudin said any official announcement on the matter would be made during the Sukma closing ceremony today at Aneka Walk, Section 14, here.
“Any prior announcements or information circulating are fake and completely untrue. Please take note and remain patient,” he said.
Yesterday, state Youth, Sports, and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi was reported as saying that the state government would consider declaring a special public holiday if the Selangor contingent emerged as the overall champion at the Games.
He said the decision would only be announced after the final medal tally had been confirmed, with Selangor currently in a strong position to secure the overall title. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan police hunt depot escapees in numbered greens, warn Kota Bharu residents against direct confrontation
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 24 — The 10 undocumented migrants who escaped from the Tanah Merah Immigration Depot, actively being pursued by authorities, are identifiable by their bright green uniforms and shaved heads.
The Kelantan Contingent Police Headquarters confirmed today that the escapees are still believed to be wearing the depot’s distinctive bright green detention attire, complete with printed identification numbers, among them 18101 and 18802.
“Their last known location was Bukit Tebu, Tanah Merah. We urge the public to report any sightings or information on their whereabouts,” the statement read.
The statement posted on the Kelantan Contingent Police Headquarters’ Facebook page said the fugitives comprise seven Thai nationals, one Indonesian, one Bangladeshi and one Rohingya.
Authorities have advised the public not to approach or take any action against the escapees if spotted, but to immediately alert the police.
Information can be directed to the Tanah Merah District Control Centre at 09-955 6222 (Tanah Merah District Police Headquarters), 09-955 6223 (Tanah Merah Police Station), or via WhatsApp at 011-2955 5518.
Meanwhile, Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat was reported yesterday as saying that the migrants had been under the custody of the Kelantan Immigration Department. — Bernama

Title: National Housing Policy: What does the policy mean for Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Malaysia’s newly unveiled National Housing Policy or Dasar Perumahan Negara (DRN) 2026-2035 aims to change how homes are planned, built, financed and managed.
The policy proposes using more detailed local data to determine where housing is needed, expanding rental and financing options, making better use of existing housing stock and strengthening the way housing projects are approved and delivered.
Here is what the policy proposes and how it helps Malaysians with housing related matters.
Supply based on on local demand
One of the main objectives is to make housing planning more responsive to local needs.
The DRN looks to ensure housing projections at the sub-district and district level, take into account existing housing supply, vacant units, housing types, household income and price categories.
Housing and transport planning would also be better coordinated, including through a proposed study on Transit-Oriented Development (TOD).
The aim is for homes to be built where people need them and are connected to jobs, transport and essential services.
Unsold homes would be taken into account
The DRN will look at strengthening housing development approvals by considering existing housing stock and completed but unsold units according to locality.
The policy will also make available a feasibility study on renting out completed but unsold homes instead of relying solely on sales.
This would make better use of existing housing stock while allowing authorities to consider actual local supply before approving more projects.
Affordability measured by location
The DRN proposes assessing the affordability of both buying and renting according to locality, alongside new guidelines for affordable housing.
It also proposes a strategic study on affordable housing needs and provision.
The approach recognises that affordability differs between locations depending on household incomes, property prices and rents.
More ways to access a home
The DRN proposes expanding access to housing beyond conventional home ownership.
These include:
Rent-to-own guidelines;
Affordable rental schemes by private developers;
Incentives for developers to provide affordable rental housing;
Shared ownership schemes;
Financing mechanisms for community- and cooperative-led housing; and
Long-term fixed-rate mortgage products.
It also proposes improving access to schemes such as Skim Jaminan Kredit Perumahan (SJKP), stepped financing and government assistance programmes:
A more formal rental market
For tenants, the policy proposes a framework for residential tenancies, including:
A Residential Tenancy Act;
A residential tenancy registration system;
E-tenancy agreements; and
Rental initiatives linked to the registration system.
The aim is to create a more structured rental market rather than leaving tenancy arrangements entirely to individual agreements between landlords and tenants.
More targeted housing for different groups
The DRN proposes housing measures based on demographic needs, including financing schemes for senior citizens, grants to modify homes for senior citizens and persons with disabilities, and different housing types according to location and demographics.
It also proposes transit housing for people facing transitional or emergency housing situations, a study on centralised worker accommodation, housing on wakaf land for lease and rental, and community- and cooperative-led housing.
Eligible people experiencing homelessness could also receive assistance to obtain more stable housing.
Preventing sick or abandoned projects
A major part of the government’s housing reform agenda is to prevent new housing projects from becoming sick, delayed or abandoned.
According to Housing and Local Government (KPKT) Minister Nga Kor Ming, KPKT’s special task force has resolved 1,647 sick and abandoned private housing projects worth RM153 billion, benefiting nearly 200,000 homebuyers.
Nga said the government is targeting zero abandoned housing projects by 2030, with the approach shifting towards prevention rather than waiting for projects to fail.
One of the measures is an Option to Purchase (OTP) mechanism, which Nga said will be introduced later this year.
A win-win
Under the proposed mechanism, developers and buyers would have a specified period to withdraw before proceeding with the sale and purchase.
Developers could exit if sales are weak and a project is deemed likely to fail, while buyers would receive a full refund of their deposits in such circumstances.
Buyers would also be able to withdraw during the stipulated period, subject to the applicable administrative charges or interest.
The government is also strengthening digital systems including HIMS (Housing Integrated Management System), TEDUH and electroni sale-and-purchase agreements, alongside periodic audits of Housing Development Accounts.
What is TEDUH and how can it help homebuyers?
TEDUH or “Transforming & Empowering Data Usage in Housing” is KPKT’s digital housing information portal.
The portal provides information on housing projects and allows prospective buyers to search projects by location and other criteria, while checking available information on project status and developers.
Its project-status system is linked to the HIMS, with data updated through the housing department’s system.
For buyers, this means TEDUH can provide another source of information to check a housing project before committing their money, rather than relying solely on information from a developer or sales agent.
Housing quality and maintenance
The DRN proposes stronger housing standards, including compliance with Universal Design Guidelines for new developments and greater use of modern construction technology.
It also proposes guidelines for housing maintenance and facility management.
For strata properties, the policy proposes that estimated maintenance and replacement costs over a property’s life cycle be included in sale-and-purchase agreements.
Better urban renewal plans
For ageing housing and urban renewal, the DRN proposes improved urban renewal guidelines, dilapidation reports for buildings identified for redevelopment and cost-benefit analyses (CBA) for housing redevelopment projects.
It also calls for stronger participation and protection of existing communities in redevelopment areas.
The aim is to consider not only whether a building needs to be redeveloped, but also its physical condition, the costs and benefits and the interests of existing residents.
Housing approvals and delivery could change
The DRN proposes taking local housing stock and completed unsold units into account when assessing new housing developments.
It also proposes amendments to the Uniform Building By-Laws (UBBL) and a new law covering the control and licensing of property developers.
Another significant proposal is to shift the housing delivery system from Jual-Kemudian-Bina (JKB), or sell-then-build, to Bina-Kemudian-Jual (BKJ), or build-then-sell.
A data-driven housing system
The policy proposes developing a Big Data Analytics and Visualisation system for the Housing Cluster (BDA Perumahan) and integrating housing data with systems used for development approvals and housing management.
It also proposes an index of construction costs according to house type.
These measures are intended to give policymakers better information on housing supply, demand, prices and construction costs.
How the DRN will assist Malaysians
For Malaysians looking to buy or rent, the proposed changes could affect several stages of the housing journey.
Before buying:
More localised housing data and platforms such as TEDUH could make it easier to compare projects, prices and development status.
When choosing how to own a home:
Rent-to-own, shared ownership and alternative financing could provide options for households unable to afford a conventional purchase.
When renting:
A formal tenancy framework could provide clearer rules and documentation for landlords and tenants.
After buying:
Stronger housing standards, maintenance planning and measures to prevent projects from becoming sick or abandoned are intended to reduce risks faced by homeowners.
For existing communities:
Urban-renewal measures could give greater weight to the condition of ageing buildings as well as the interests of residents affected by redevelopment.

Title: Two boys, 13 and 16, found dead after being swept away by strong currents in Sabah
Article:
KENINGAU, Aug 23 — Two teenage boys who were reported missing after being swept away by strong currents in Sungai Pegalan, Kampung Bakti here yesterday, were found dead today.
The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Centre said the body of the first victim, Jasti Gomen, 16, was found at 10.34am, while the second victim, Khend Rommel Ponce Caceres, 13, was found at 3.55pm.
“The body of the first victim was found by the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) 50 metres from the place he was reported to have been swept away, while the second victim was found 80 metres away,” the Sabah JBPM said in a statement today.
The bodies of both victims were handed over to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) for further action before the search and rescue (SAR) operation was called off at 5pm.
In the incident at about 2.30pm yesterday, both victims were reportedly bathing with their friends when they fell off the riverbank and were swept away by strong currents.
JBPM received an emergency call at 3.15pm yesterday and launched an initial search before suspending the operation at 6pm due to weather conditions and fading daylight.
The SAR operation resumed at 9am today and was divided into two search sectors, covering a three-kilometre stretch of the river surface, as well as a specialised diving operation conducted by five members of the Kuala Penyu PPDA, which began at 10.30am.
A total of 15 JBPM personnel from the Keningau and Kuala Penyu Fire and Rescue Stations were deployed to the scene.
The SAR operation also involved seven PDRM personnel, 13 Keningau Civil Defence Force personnel and five members of the local volunteer group Galon Star. — Bernama

Title: No militants have crossed into Malaysia after southern Thailand attacks, authorities say
Article:
PASIR MAS, Aug 23 — There has been no reported attempt by militants or guerrillas from Southern Thailand to cross into Kelantan so far, following last night’s coordinated bombings and violent attacks across three southern Thai provinces.
Confirming this, Southeast Brigade Commander of the General Operations Force (PGA) SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said border security along the Malaysia-Thailand frontier is being tightened as a precaution, with front-line personnel on high alert for any potential infiltration attempts.
“We are constantly reinforcing border controls and reminding our front-line teams to stay vigilant. We will act swiftly if there are any incidents or attempts to enter,” he told Bernama today.
He noted that, as of now, the only persistent issue at the border remains the entry of undocumented migrants.
On cooperation with Thai authorities, Ahmad Radzi said bilateral relations are strong, with the Regional Border Committee (RBC) serving as an effective platform for intelligence-sharing and coordination.
He said the RBC meeting is scheduled for Sept 1 to 3 in Hat Yai, Thailand, and will be attended by Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat, Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah, the acting Perlis police chief, himself, and Malaysian Armed Forces representatives.
“We maintain a continuous exchange of intelligence, and our cooperation with Thai authorities has always been solid,” he emphasised.
The RBC, he added, operates through six working groups covering border management, land affairs, disaster response, and intelligence, all designed to strengthen security collaboration between Malaysia and Thailand.
On the ground, a Bernama check in Pekan Rantau Panjang near the border today found that PGA personnel have intensified patrols and surveillance at strategic spots, particularly along key access routes leading into the frontier.
Meanwhile, Mohd Yusoff confirmed today that no Malaysians were caught in last night’s bombings and violence across three southern Thai provinces.
He advised Malaysians to remain cautious and postpone non-essential travel to Thailand until the situation stabilises.
Narathiwat province had been placed under a curfew from 10.15pm last night until 5am today, following reports of over 50 bombings, arson targeting local government offices and tyre-burning.
The powerful explosions, heard from Narathiwat last night, sent shockwaves through border communities, rattling homes and raising alarm among residents in Kampung Lubok Gong and Kampung Tersang in Rantau Panjang. — Bernama

Title: October Sarawak assembly sitting no sign of November state election, says Abdul Karim
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 23 — The possibility of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting being brought forward to October is not an indication that the next state election will be held in November, said Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.
He said the DUN normally sits at least twice a year, and therefore the possible change from November to October should not be linked to speculation over the timing of the state election.
“I also see it that way. Usually, the sitting is held in November. This time, it may be held in October after the National Budget.
“It is not surprising because in Sarawak, the Assembly usually sits twice a year,” he said when met after watching a Sukma XXII diving event at the Darul Ehsan Aquatic Centre here on Sunday.
When asked to comment about speculation that the Sarawak election could be held in November if the Assembly sitting is brought forward, Abdul Karim said he did not view the matter from that perspective.
“That is the premier’s prerogative. If it is brought forward, there may be certain reasons for it, but I do not see it from that perspective. I see it more as part of the process where the Assembly needs to sit at least twice a year,” he said.
Meanwhile, Abdul Karim said holding the state election using 99 DUN seats by the end of this year could face constraints due to the time required for the delineation process.
He said the Election Commission (EC) would first need to display the proposed electoral boundaries, which he believed would take at least three months before the subsequent process could be carried out.
“Technically, I think the process would be quite difficult. It is not that it cannot be done, because I see that the EC already intends to display the proposed number of seats.
“But the problem is that the process of displaying them takes time. At least three months, if I am not mistaken,” he said.
He said the period may not be sufficient to enable the Sarawak election to be held using the 99 seats approved by the Sarawak Legislative Assembly.
According to him, the Bill to increase the number of DUN seats from 82 to 99 had been passed with almost unanimous support and was now awaiting the next processes involving the EC and Parliament.
“I was the one who tabled the Bill previously. It was passed with almost unanimous support by the Legislative Assembly.
“It is only awaiting the EC and confirmation in Parliament. But the timeframe and process may not allow it to be held before the end of this year,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Care should not fall on families alone, says Nancy as welfare spending hits RM728m
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 23 — The Social Welfare Department (JKM) has spent about RM728.5 million to support the welfare of senior citizens, persons with disabilities (PwD) and chronic patients nationwide as of June this year.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the allocation was channelled through the Senior Citizen Assistance (BWE) and the Assistance for Care of Bedridden Persons with Disabilities and Bedridden Chronic Patients (BPT).
“To ease the burden on families, the Social Welfare Department also assists with the care of bedridden persons with disabilities, bedridden chronic patients and non-bedridden chronic patients who meet the eligibility criteria.
“As of June 2026, a total of 42,036 recipients nationwide had received this assistance, involving expenditure of more than RM119.5 million,” she said when officiating the Sarawak-level SPeKTRUM Caregiver Support Programme at the state branch of Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP) here today.
Nancy said during the same period, BWE was channelled to 170,133 recipients nationwide, involving expenditure of more than RM609 million.
On the distribution in Sarawak, she said 23,034 senior citizens in the state had benefited from BWE, involving an allocation of more than RM94.3 million, while more than RM10.4 million had been channelled to 3,235 BPT recipients in the state.
Meanwhile, Nancy stressed that strengthening the country’s care ecosystem was important, particularly to ensure the welfare of caregivers looking after these groups was also safeguarded.
She said the responsibility of caring for those who were frail or bedridden should not rest solely on families without strong support from various quarters.
“That is why, through SPeKTRUM, caregivers are provided with training, psychosocial support and motivation so that they can provide the best care without neglecting their own health,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Haze watch: Sungai Petani, Johan Setia worsen as five more areas in Malaysia edge towards unhealthy levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — The haze picture shifted across peninsular Malaysia this afternoon, with Sungai Petani worsening and five other areas creeping towards unhealthy levels, while Sarawak remained the country’s worst-affected region.
Worsening
Sungai Petani in Kedah recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 153 at 5pm, up from 140 at 9am.
Johan Setia in Selangor also worsened slightly, climbing from 157 to 160 and remaining the highest reading in the peninsula.
Improving
Taiping in Perak, meanwhile, improved from 121 at 9am to 112 at 5pm, but remained in the unhealthy category.
Creeping towards unhealthy
Five locations were now hovering close to the unhealthy threshold, with Klang recording 95, Banting and Putrajaya 93 each, Bukit Rambai in Melaka 92 and Nilai in Negeri Sembilan 91.
All five remained in the moderate category but were within 10 points of the unhealthy threshold.
Sarawak still worst hit
Sarawak continued to record the country’s highest API readings, although all four affected locations showed slight improvements compared with this morning.
Serian remained the worst affected at 186, down from 194 at 9am, followed by Kuching at 176 from 183, while Samarahan eased from 175 to 173 and Sri Aman from 177 to 173.
What the numbers mean
API readings of 0 to 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and above 300 as hazardous.
The Department of Environment is monitoring air quality through 68 stations nationwide, with readings updated hourly.
The latest readings come as the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre continues to monitor hotspot activity and smoke plumes in parts of the region, with prevailing winds blowing from the southeast.

Title: Kemaman police detain man over alleged seditious Facebook post against Royal Institution and govt
Article:
CHUKAI, Aug 23 — Police have detained a man suspected of making a seditious and insulting Facebook post against the Royal Institution, the Malaysian government and a security agency.
Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the 39-year-old man was arrested in Damansara Damai, Petaling Jaya, Selangor on Wednesday, and a mobile phone and two SIM cards were seized.
“The seized items have been handed over to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for digital forensic analysis,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Razi said the man has been remanded until Wednesday to assist in the investigation under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
On Aug 15, the media reported that police were investigating the owner of the Facebook account ‘Ahmad Mu’min’ over a post that contained seditious and insulting elements against the Royal Institution, the Malaysian Government, and the security agency. — Bernama

Title: Terengganu’s Teluk Kalong Beach hit by coal pollution again, second incident this year
Article:
CHUKAI, Aug 23 — Teluk Kalong Beach here has once again been affected by coal pollution over the past three days, believed to have originated from a barge that broke apart near the beach last January.
A local resident, Azhar Ngah, 64, said the black solid material had been washed ashore by the tide, covering a 300-metre stretch of coastline and affecting the cleanliness and scenic appeal of the recreational area.
He said the beach had experienced similar pollution last January following a coal spill from a barge, although cleanup operations were subsequently carried out by the parties involved.
“I hope the authorities will immediately carry out cleanup operations to remove the coal debris, ensuring the cleanliness of the beach as well as the safety and well-being of fishermen and visitors,” he told Bernama when met at Teluk Kalong Beach today.
Meanwhile, fisherman Mohamad Azrul Naim Rahim, 36, expressed concern over the beach’s condition, which he said had previously been clean but had been covered with black solid material for the past three days.
However, he said the current coal pollution was not as severe as the incident last January, with a smaller volume of debris washed ashore and a more limited affected area.
“Nevertheless, we are concerned that the coal spillage from the barge could worsen if the authorities fail to take immediate action,” he said.
Meanwhile, Terengganu Tourism, Culture, Environment and Climate Change Committee chairman Datuk Razali Idris said he had instructed the Kemaman Municipal Council (MPK), Department of Environment (DOE) and Marine Department Malaysia to investigate the source of the coal pollution, which is the second such incident reported at the beach this year.
He said the relevant agencies had also been directed to immediately clear the coal debris from the beach to ensure the coastal area was clean, safe and conducive for visitors.
“Cleanup operations must be carried out immediately as the beach is a popular tourist destination,” he said.
On January 12, media reports stated that Teluk Kalong Beach had been polluted by coal believed to have originated from a cargo spill after a barge drifted and sank in the area. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Malaysia should build full ecosystem to lead global Muslim travel economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Malaysia must move beyond being the world’s leading Muslim-friendly destination and become a global hub for the Muslim travel economy, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said the country should build an ecosystem that connects tourism with halal innovation, trade, technology and local enterprises, while creating opportunities for entrepreneurs, small businesses and communities.
“A traveller contributes far more than a hotel booking. Every journey creates demand for transport, food, retail, entertainment, digital services, local products and cultural experiences. Tourism should therefore be viewed as an economic multiplier,” he said.
He said this in his keynote address at the Ministers and Chief Executive Officers Summit held in conjunction with the World Islamic Tourism & Trade Expo (WITEX) 2026 at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL) today.
Also present was Malaysia Tourism Agency Association (MATA) president and WITEX 2026 organising chairman Datuk Seri Dr Mohd Khalid Harun.
Ahmad Zahid said international Muslim arrivals reached 196 million in 2025 and are projected to rise to 262 million by 2030, with travel expenditure estimated at USD310 billion.
He said Muslim travellers now expect more than halal food, prayer facilities and suitable accommodation, as they also travel for business, wellness, culture, nature and adventure.
He added that Malaysia must adopt new technologies, develop talent through Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) and strengthen halal and Muslim-friendly standards to remain competitive in the global Muslim travel market.
Speaking to reporters afterwards, Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia needed to diversify its Islamic tourism products and offer them throughout the year to meet the changing preferences of Muslim tourists.
“Malaysia has great potential in Islamic tourism, not only during specific events or occasions such as Aidiladha, Aidilfitri or Ramadan, but throughout the year, when we can offer various Islamic tourism packages,” he said.
On tourists from West Asia, he said developments in the region had prompted many of them to choose Southeast Asia; hence, efforts should be intensified to attract more of these tourists to Malaysia through platforms such as WITEX.
The fourth edition of WITEX 2026, organised by MATA, is being held from Aug 21 to 23, bringing together industry players in Islamic tourism, halal trade, investment, innovation and culture. — Bernama

Title: MCMC, Selangor to expand filtered internet service to public premises and private institutions, says exco
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 23 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with the Selangor state government, plans to expand its filtered internet service to public premises and private higher learning institutions (IPTS).
Selangor Islamic Affairs and Innovation Culture Committee chairman Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the move followed the success of a pilot project implemented at mosques in the state to curb the spread of negative content.
He said content filtering was important to ensure digital access was not misused during important activities such as prayers and learning sessions.
“If we install a filtering system at mosques to prevent children from playing online games during prayer times, the same approach will be extended to IPTS and related public residences,” he told reporters after officiating the Petaling Jaya District Safe Internet Campaign Community Carnival 2026 at Kampung Lindungan here today.
On cyber threats, Mohammad Fahmi said 35,073 online scam cases were recorded as of June, involving losses of RM951.7 million, with investment scams accounting for RM413.8 million.
“Losses amounting to nearly RM1 billion involve people’s life savings. Therefore, the public needs to practise the concept of ‘tabayyun’ or careful verification through the principles of ‘Check Before Clicking, Think Before Sharing’,” he said.
He also proposed that authorities use artificial intelligence (AI) to automatically screen keywords or fake accounts to combat cyberbullying and extreme content without waiting for public complaints.
Earlier, the carnival organised by MCMC attracted more than 300 visitors and featured various interactive activities, including aerobics, a Mobile Legends e-sports competition and cybersecurity awareness briefings.
Visitor Nor Syuhadah Maznan, 28, said the combination of talent-based activities and cyber advocacy made digital safety messages more relaxed and easier for the community to understand.
“The government’s efforts should continue for the safety of the younger generation, as online content today often crosses boundaries unintentionally,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Selangor may declare holiday if host contingent emerge overall Sukma champions, says exco
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 23 — The Selangor government will consider declaring an occasional holiday if the host contingent emerge overall champions at the ongoing Malaysia Games (SUKMA) 2026.
State Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi said the matter would only be announced after the medal tally is finalised, with the Selangor contingent looking well placed to end the Games on a high.
“We will propose the holiday to Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari for his consideration. If we emerge overall champions, perhaps an incentive could be considered for the people of Selangor.
“As for incentives for athletes who perform well, Insya-Allah, we will work on that after SUKMA is over,” he told a press conference on the latest developments at SUKMA Selangor at the Selangor State Sports Council building here today.
Najwan said that as of 2.50 pm today, Selangor had collected 85 gold medals, with the latest contributed by, among others, the women’s Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) esports team, women’s 3m springboard diving, women’s singles table tennis and men’s singles lawn bowls.
“However, I would also like to remind the athletes to remain focused. We have roughly a day and a half left before the SUKMA competition ends, so give it your best. Winning or losing is part and parcel of competition,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Got 20,000 tech engineers, but where are the investors? Jerejak may have the answer, says Bayan Baru MP
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 23 — Penang’s plan to turn part of Pulau Jerejak into a financial and lifestyle hub is being pitched as a way to give the state’s technology start-ups something they have long lacked — access to investors.
Bayan Baru MP Sim Tze Tzin said the proposed 32-hectare development could bring venture capitalists, private equity firms, bankers and technology investors closer to the engineers driving Penang’s semiconductor industry,
The Star
reported.
“Penang needs venture capitalists, private equity funds, bankers and technology investors to set up offices in one location so that they can interact with technology companies and potentially channel funding into new ventures,” he told reporters in Sungai Nibong yesterday.
Sim said Penang has about 20,000 integrated circuit design engineers, many of whom remain salaried employees because they lack investors to help them establish their own companies.
He said clustering investors and technology companies in one place could create the kind of interaction needed to turn engineering talent into new businesses, likening the proposed ecosystem to Silicon Valley in the US.
Sim, who lived in Silicon Valley for six years, said regular interaction between engineers, entrepreneurs and investors could help generate new ideas and spur the growth of Penang’s technology sector.
The proposed development by Tropical Island Resort is to include a financial centre, resort, serviced apartments and hotels, with the aim of creating an ecosystem to attract investment into the state’s technology and semiconductor industries.
Bayan Baru MP Sim Tze Tzin believes Pulau Jerejak is the answer to Penang’s tech funding gap. — FIle picture by Shafwan Zaidon
Sim said development would be subject to restrictions on building height and density, while 85 per cent of Pulau Jerejak’s 360-hectare area remains gazetted as forest reserve.
He also said the state government had asked the developer to restore several heritage sites on the island, which has a history as a quarantine and medical site before later becoming a detention centre.
Work on a 1km elevated bridge linking Pulau Jerejak with Penang island is expected to begin with road-widening works next month and be completed by March 2029.
The RM500 million bridge will have two lanes in each direction, as well as pedestrian and cycling lanes, and will connect the area near Jambatan Harapan and Queensbay Mall to the island.
Sim said the developer had agreed to his proposal for the bridge to become an iconic landmark, with two international architects and one local architect to be appointed for its design.
The bridge is expected to provide direct road access to Pulau Jerejak, which currently relies on boat services, while making the island more accessible to tourists.

Title: PM approves additional RM1m for Hindu crematorium project in Bagan, says PHEB
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Aug 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional RM1 million allocation to the Penang State Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) for the construction of a modern Hindu crematorium in Bagan here,  said PHEB chairman RSN Rayer.
He said the additional allocation brought the total funding for the project to RM2.5 million, up from the RM1.5 million previously approved by Anwar.
He said the original RM1.5 million allocation was found to be insufficient to implement the project, which is much needed by the Hindu community, particularly in Seberang Perai. It will be Penang’s second modern electric crematorium, after the facility in Batu Lanchang.
“This additional approval reflects the concern and commitment of the Madani Government and the Prime Minister in ensuring that the needs of Malaysia’s multiracial and multireligious communities are given fair attention,” he said at a press conference at the project site on Jalan Siram today.
Also present were Bagan Member of Parliament Lim Guan Eng and Bagan Dalam state assemblyman Kumaran Krishnan.
Meanwhile, Kumaran said the crematorium was important in providing a more organised, suitable and comfortable facility for the Hindu community to perform final rites according to their customs and religious beliefs.
He said the facility would also reduce the reliance of the Hindu community in Seberang Perai on crematorium facilities located farther away.
“This is a long-term facility for the benefit of the Hindu community, particularly in Seberang Perai and the surrounding areas,” he said.
Kumaran said the approval of the additional allocation was the result of a joint application and efforts by Lim and Rayer, who had written to Anwar to seek additional funding to ensure that the project could be implemented more comprehensively.
He said the tender process for the construction of the approximately 4,000-square-foot crematorium had been opened, and the project was expected to be fully completed by the middle of next year. — Bernama

Title: Post-mortem shows 11-year-old tahfiz participant found in Lenggeng pond died from drowning, police say no signs of abuse
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 23 — An 11-year-old boy who was found in a pond near a foundation centre in Kampung Kapal, Lenggeng early today died from drowning, resulting in a lack of oxygen, police said.
Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said the finding was made after a post-mortem at the Forensic Department of Hospital Tuanku Ja’afar here, which began at 9.30am and lasted more than two hours,
Harian Metro
reported this afternoon.
“External and internal examinations of the victim’s body also found no other injuries or signs indicating abuse,” the senior police officer was quoted as saying.
The boy had been reported missing while taking part in a
tahfiz
– a Quran memorisation – programme before he was found in a weak condition in a pond near the site.
Police received a report about his disappearance at 12.28am and launched a search with the assistance of relevant agencies around the area.
The boy was found in the pond in a weak condition and given resuscitation before further medical examination was carried out.
He was later pronounced dead by a medical officer from the Lenggeng Health Clinic.

Title: After southern Thailand blasts, Wisma Putra tells Malaysians to think twice before crossing border
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Malaysians planning to travel to or cross into southern Thailand have been urged to exercise heightened caution and postpone non-essential trips following a wave of bomb blasts and other attacks across the region last night.
The Foreign Ministry, also called Wisma Putra, said no Malaysians had been reported affected by the incidents in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, but advised those residing in, travelling through or planning trips to the affected areas to remain vigilant and follow local security instructions.
“Malaysians residing in, travelling through, or intending to travel to and from the southern border provinces of Thailand are strongly advised to exercise heightened caution, remain vigilant, and strictly observe all safety advisories, curfews, and security instructions implemented by local authorities,” it said in a media advisory today.
The advisory came after a Malaysian visitor to Sungai Golok found himself stranded in the Thai border town when explosions began at about 9pm, with security forces shutting roads and preventing vehicles from reaching the border complex.
Residents in Kelantan border towns like Rantau Panjang, Pengkalan Kubor and Pasir Mas also said the blasts were powerful enough to be heard and, in some homes, felt , with one resident saying his house walls shook.
The attacks were reported across Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, with Thai authorities reporting 51 incidents by midnight, including explosions, arson and attacks on public facilities, while curfews and heightened security measures were imposed in affected areas.
Wisma Putra said the Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok and Consulate General in Songkhla were maintaining close contact with Thai authorities to monitor developments and safeguard Malaysians in the country.
Malaysians in Thailand have also been urged to register and regularly update their contact details through the ministry’s e-Konsular portal to facilitate communication and consular assistance.
The ministry said Malaysians requiring emergency consular assistance could contact the embassy in Bangkok or the consulate general in Songkhla through their respective hotlines.

Title: IIUM ends ties with academic behind controversial Roman-Malay shipbuilding claim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) has confirmed that controversial academic Solehah Yaacob is no longer with the university, months after she drew public scrutiny over claims that ancient Romans learned shipbuilding from Malays and that meteor activity may explain Kedah’s iron ore deposits.
The university said Solehah’s academic service was terminated on April 27, and she is no longer a professor or representative of IIUM in any official capacity, local news outlets reported today, citing a statement from IIUM’s Office of Communication, Advocacy and Promotion.
The university said Solehah was also barred from using any official title, position or affiliation linking her to IIUM in promotional materials, media reports, publications, advertisements, social media content, publicity materials or other forms of public dissemination.
IIUM said the clarification was necessary to prevent confusion over Solehah’s status and protect the university’s institutional integrity in academic representation.
Solehah, who previously served as an Arabic language and linguistics academic at IIUM, first attracted widespread attention last year after claiming that ancient Romans may have learned shipbuilding techniques from Malay seafarers.
The claim prompted Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir to advise university academics to avoid making claims beyond their areas of expertise, while IIUM had previously stressed that her views did not represent the university’s official position.
More recently, Solehah presented a theory linking Kedah’s abundance of iron ore to meteor activity in ancient times, again drawing debate over the claim.
